title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES PUBLIC PROGRAMME AT JAGDALPUR, CHHATTISGARH ON THE OCCASION OF BASTAR DUSSEHRA
subtitle: LET US DRAW VALUABLE LESSONS FROM THE NATURE-NURTURING LIFESTYLE OF THE TRIBAL COMMUNITY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 4:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced and addressed a public programme at Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh today (October 23, 2026) on the occasion of Bastar Dussehra.
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Bastar Dussehra serves as a vibrant symbol of Chhattisgarh’s cultural pride and collective faith. The manner in which the entire community participates in the Bastar Dussehra festival is truly extraordinary. Various rituals of this festival foster a deep sense of connection and kinship among different sections of society.
The President said that Chhattisgarh has long endured the scourge of Naxalism. Through the coordinated efforts of the central and state governments, the region has been freed from the menace of Naxal violence and is now advancing rapidly along the path of progress. She was happy to note that in recent times, initiatives to provide financial support to tribal entrepreneurs and connect them with markets have been further accelerated. She expressed confidence that these efforts will prove instrumental in achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047 through equitable and inclusive development.
The President added that tribal communities worship nature which is life-giving. In the journey of development, we should draw valuable lessons from the nature-nurturing lifestyle of the tribal community. She underlined the importance of preserving and nurturing the nature.
Before the public programme, the President interacted with the local Manjhi and Chalki in the Muriya Darbar. She also visited the Rangoli and Dussehra exhibition at Jagdalpur.
Earlier, the President performed darshan and pooja at Maa Danteshwari Temple at Jagdalpur.

title: Innovations and Emerging Technologies Should Benefit All Humanity, Not Be the Exclusive Property of Any One Country: Vice-President
subtitle:
“Advantage India is Advantage to Humanity”: Vice-President says Viksit Bharat is both an aspiration and a responsibility, calling for collective participation in nation-building

India’s civilisational heritage, democratic traditions and technological capabilities constitute its unique strengths: Vice-President

Vice-President releases Anil Antony’s  ‘Advantage India: Reshaping the Future for an Equitable World’ at Uprashtrapati Bhawan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today released the book ‘Advantage India: Reshaping the Future for an Equitable World’, authored by Shri Anil K. Antony at Uprashtrapati Bhawan, New Delhi.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released ‘Advantage India: Reshaping the Future for an Equitable World’, authored by Shri Anil K. Antony, at Uprashtrapati Bhawan today.

He highlighted India’s remarkable transformation, civilisational heritage, democratic traditions, technological advancements and growing global influence. Emphasising the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, he called upon young Indians to contribute actively to nation-building.

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India,Professor Ajay Sood; Economist and Member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council,Dr. Shamika Ravi; and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 23, 2026
Congratulating the author and Rupa Publications on the publication, the Vice-President said that the book captures India’s remarkable transformation and explores the opportunities before the nation in a rapidly changing world. Drawing upon his experience in technology, business and public policy, Shri Antony examines India’s emerging strengths and its growing role in the international order, he noted.
Highlighting India’s unique strengths, the Vice-President said that the country’s civilisational heritage, democratic traditions, demographic dividend, growing economy, robust institutions and expanding technological capabilities together constitute its distinctive advantage.
The Vice-President highlighted the transformative journey of India under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, noting that more than 25 crore people have been lifted out of absolute poverty. He said that initiatives in education, housing, sanitation, healthcare and food security have enhanced the dignity and social security of millions of citizens.
Emphasising the importance of inclusive development, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the empowerment of women, youth, farmers and underprivileged sections remains central to India’s progress. The emergence of more than three crore Lakhpati Didis reflects the success of women-led development, he observed. He also highlighted the expansion of educational and healthcare infrastructure through new IITs, AIIMS, medical colleges and other higher educational institutions, alongside major improvements in connectivity through Vande Bharat trains, airports, highways and railway stations.
Recalling the evolution of technology in India, the Vice-President said that while the advent of computers had initially generated apprehension, India subsequently emerged as a global IT powerhouse. Emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning present similar opportunities for the country today, he said, adding that leadership plays a crucial role in harnessing technology for societal progress.
Referring to the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat, the Vice-President said that India has made significant strides in indigenous manufacturing across sectors. Recalling his recent commissioning of INS Samarthak, an indigenous multipurpose vessel, he said that the achievement exemplifies the growing capabilities of India’s domestic defence production.
Turning to India’s expanding international role, the Vice-President observed that Indian diplomacy has undergone a significant transformation, characterised by greater engagement, growing influence and renewed confidence. He recalled India’s leadership during its G20 Presidency and its role in advancing the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the world is one family. He also highlighted India’s contribution to the inclusion of the African Union in the G20 and its emergence as a voice for the Global South.
Emphasising that Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam is more than a slogan and represents a guiding philosophy of Bharat, the Vice-President cited India’s response during the COVID-19 pandemic. He noted that India not only undertook a nationwide vaccination drive but also extended life-saving vaccines to more than 100 countries, reflecting the country’s commitment to global solidarity and service to humanity.
The Vice-President emphasised that “Advantage India is Advantage to Humanity.” He stated that all sovereign countries are equal and must be treated equally. He said “Any new innovation or technological advancement should benefit the whole of humanity and should not remain the exclusive property of any one country”. He called for a more equitable approach to technological progress, ensuring that its benefits are shared for the collective welfare of humanity.
The Vice-President said that the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 is both an aspiration and a responsibility, requiring a collective commitment to the principle of Rashtra Pratham. Nation-building, he stressed, cannot be accomplished by the government alone and calls for the active participation of every citizen.
Expressing hope that the book would inspire young Indians to engage more deeply with technology, public policy, economics, international relations and nation-building, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan congratulated Shri Anil K. Antony and extended his best wishes to the author, publisher and everyone associated with the publication.
Professor Ajay Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India; Dr. Shamika Ravi, economist and Member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council; Shri Anil K. Antony, author; Shri Kapish Mehra, Managing Editor, Rupa Publications, diplomats and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: Prime Minister  Shri Narendra Modi  inaugurates Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan
subtitle:
The Chinmaya Mission has spent decades serving communities and sharing India's spiritual wisdom with the world: PM

Chinmaya Mission is not just an institution; it is a profound 'Chinmaya' thought, established by a 'Chinmaya' sage; Its decades-long journey has been brimming with 'Chinmaya' resolves; and that which is 'Chinmaya', is naturally immortal and full of eternal nectar: PM

Our nation is the cradle of our culture; This very nation is the foundation of our existence: PM

Driven by the efforts of the Chinmaya Mission, millions of youth today are serving as India's cultural brand ambassadors; These youth are passing on Indian values to the new generation: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister described his participation as a deeply spiritual experience born of the saints' affection and blessings. Emphasizing that the Chinmaya Mission is not a mere institution but an immortal consciousness founded by a sage and driven by decades of sacred resolutions, he noted the profound aptness of the celebration's title.
Reflecting on how modern technology heightened the emotional resonance of the event through a Holobot interaction with Revered Gurudev Swami Chinmayananda, the Prime Minister shared that the experience transported him 33 years back to his 1993 meeting with the spiritual leader in Vadodara. Recalling Gurudev’s warmth, conversation, and blessings as if standing in his direct presence once more, he expressed heartfelt gratitude to the Mission’s members for creating such a moving tribute."For me, this is a very emotional experience,” remarked PM Modi.
Recounting his February-March 1993 visit to invite Swami Chinmayananda to Chicago for the centenary of the Parliament of the World's Religions,marking 100 years of Swami Vivekananda’s historic address,the Prime Minister noted how Gurudev tirelessly rallied people across America for the event before passing away in San Diego on August 3. Remembering how deeply Gurudev's absence was felt at the Chicago gathering on September 11, he recalled their final conversation, which centered on cultivating youth power."Its main essence was the building of youth power, and building a strong and capable India through youth power!” affirmed Shri Modi.
Tracing his 25-year journey of continuous service as a head of government since becoming the Chief Minister of Gujarat a few years after that meeting, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's youth have remained at the heart of his policies. He lauded the young volunteers of the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav for shouldering major responsibilities and covering 40,000 kilometers over 300 days to engage with over one lakh young citizens."I congratulate the entire team for this wonderful effort as well,” lauded PM Modi.
Invoking the Upanishadic dictum “Vayam Amritasya Putrah” (We are the children of immortality), the Prime Minister explained that India has endured for millennia as a seeker of knowledge and light because its consciousness and wisdom are immortal, which inspired him on the 75th anniversary of Independence to call for an Amrit Mahotsav that serves both as a launchpad for a Viksit Bharat and a revival of India's millennia-old concern for humanity. Noting how numerous spiritual, cultural, and social bodies have since taken sacred pledges at key milestones, he celebrated the Chinmaya Mission’s integration into the nation's Amrit Kaal campaign. "This indeed is the real proof of our being Amritasya Putrah,” asserted Shri Modi.
Citing the Vedic call "Vayam Rashtre Jagriyama Purohitah" to awaken and elevate the nation, the Prime Minister highlighted how Swami Chinmayananda spoke as vocally on national priorities as he did on spirituality, teaching that because the nation is the cradle of our culture and existence, spiritual growth must fuel personal growth and national progress. To instill national self-respect, Swamiji launched the Gita Gyana Yagna to bring the Upanishads, Vedanta, and scriptures to the masses, resulting today in lakhs of Chinmaya Mission youth passing on Indian values as cultural brand ambassadors."This contribution of Revered Gurudev is an important chapter in India's cultural and spiritual renaissance,” affirmed PM Modi.
Recalling the release of a commemorative coin during Gurudev’s birth centenary in 2015, the Prime Minister described Swamiji’s life as a remarkable confluence of Gyana, Karma, and Bhakti that fulfilled his Guru Swami Sivananda’s blessing to “Go, roar like a lion.” He noted that Swamiji's inner conviction left an indelible mark on listeners, while his 'Art of Man Making' radio program guided countless lives."The self-confidence that was in his voice, the inner strength that was there, used to leave an imprint of his thoughts on everyone's heart,” remarked Shri Modi.
Observing that the mission of great personalities endures well beyond their lifetime, the Prime Minister highlighted the expansive education network established by the Chinmaya Mission. He pointed out that over 100 Chinmaya educational institutions are currently shaping the future of lakhs of students across the country."They are getting modern education in these institutions, and they are also imbibing Indian values,” noted PM Modi.
Aligning contemporary governance with the post-independence vision of thinkers like Swami Chinmayananda, the Prime Minister stated that the country is actively fulfilling its duty to modernize academics for a New India. He highlighted the introduction of the National Education Policy, which integrates the Indian knowledge tradition, education in the mother tongue, modern science, and technology. “In this new education policy, importance has been given to all of these,” asserted Shri Modi.
Spotlighting Swamiji’s lifelong dedication to preserving Indian heritage, the Prime Minister recalled how Gurudev stood firmly behind Eknath Ranade’s resolve to build the Vivekananda Rock Memorial in the sea at Kanyakumari and donated the very first financial contribution toward the project. He noted that the monument now serves as a beacon of inspiration for millions globally."Another mission of Swamiji's life was pride in Indian heritage, and its preservation!” observed PM Modi.
Detailing the sweeping cultural renaissance spanning the nation from North to South and East to West, the Prime Minister pointed to the grand revitalization of Kashi Vishwanath Dham, the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya, Ujjain’s Mahakal Mahalok, Kedarnath, and Badrinath, alongside the inclusion of cultural sites on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Contrasting previous eras when stolen Indian antiquities were sold abroad without resistance, he highlighted the repatriation of heritage artifacts over the last dozen years."In the past 12 years, we have also brought back more than six hundred and fifty such ancient idols,” noted Shri Modi.
Drawing a parallel between Swamiji taking Indian philosophy to the world and International Yoga Day uniting the globe with India today, the Prime Minister emphasized that the nation's renewed pride in its heritage and liberation from a colonial mindset prove it is advancing on the path envisioned by ancient sages and patriots. He stressed that their intellectual legacy remains the country's greatest strength on this journey."This self-confidence of pride in our heritage and this assurance of freedom from the mentality of slavery is proof of the fact that the country is now moving forward on that path,” asserted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that while various organizations pursue distinct goals, all paths ultimately converge on the singular destination of national development and glory, the Prime Minister noted that just as Swami Chinmayananda tailored his resolutions to the challenges of his era, today's generation must address modern societal distortions and challenges. He called for proactive efforts to unite society against divisive forces, promote self-reliance, and connect every citizen with the 2047 Viksit Bharat goal."Today, we have to unite society against divisive forces,” asserted Shri Modi.
Pointing out the historic convergence in 2047 when India’s centenary of Independence will coincide with the centenary period of the Chinmaya Mission, the Prime Minister stated that both journeys share identical goals and must advance in tandem. Expressing full faith that the Mission's global family of Acharyas, seekers, and volunteers will leverage Gurudev's legacy and decades of experience to help build a Viksit Bharat,  and offered his final festive greetings."Meaning, the centenary journey of the Chinmaya Mission and the journey of a Viksit Bharat will move forward together,” affirmed PM Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's address at the inauguration of Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 1:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Most revered Pujya Swami Tejomayananda ji, Pujya Swami Swaroopananda ji, Pujya Swami Mitrananda ji, Pujya Swami Viviktananda ji, all revered saints, Acharyas, all dedicated sevaks of Chinmaya Mission, devotees and seekers who have arrived from across the country and abroad, ladies and gentlemen.
Courtesy of all of you, today I have had the opportunity to participate in the Amrit Mahotsav of Chinmaya Mission. This is a unique spiritual experience. This is the special affection and blessing of our saints towards me. Because the Chinmaya Mission is not merely an institution; it is a Chinmaya ideal, which was established by a Chinmaya Rishi. Its journey over several decades has also been replete with pure, conscious resolutions. And whatever is Chinmaya is naturally immortal and imbued with nectar. Therefore, today at Bharat Mandapam, the name of this event - 'Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav' - is equally meaningful. I extend my heartiest congratulations on the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav to the saints and Acharyas associated with the Chinmaya Mission across the globe, and to lakhs of seekers and followers.
Friends,
The feeling that arose in my heart upon arriving here today was made even more vibrant through modern technology. The darshan of Pujya Gurudev Swami Chinmayananda ji in this form, the privilege of conversing with his holobot, made it feel as though I had travelled 33 years back in time. My meeting with Gurudev in Vadodara in 1993, the conversation with him, his affection, his blessings - today everything reappeared before my eyes once again. For a moment, it felt as though I was once again in the direct physical presence of Gurudev. For me, this is a deeply emotional experience. I thank all the members of Chinmaya Mission from the bottom of my heart for this wonderful experience, and express my gratitude to them.
Friends,
Around February-March in 1993, I met Pujya Gurudev; I had gone to invite him to the centenary celebrations of the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago, USA. At that very time, 100 years of Swami Vivekananda ji's historic address were being marked. Pujya Gurudev accepted the invitation; Pujya Gurudev went to America, and across various programmes there, he consistently made people aware of the centenary celebrations of the World's Parliament of Religions and inspired them to take part. But destiny had ordained otherwise. Just a few weeks prior to the Parliament of Religions, on 3 August, Gurudev shed his mortal body in San Diego, America, leaving all of us behind. When the Parliament of Religions took place in Chicago on 11 September, fortunately, I was there. All of us felt the absence of Pujya Gurudev. Many words spoken by Gurudev kept echoing in my mind. The profound discussion that took place during my last meeting with him remains etched in my memory even today. Its core sentiment was: the building of youth power! And, through youth power, the creation of an empowered and capable India.
Friends,
A few years after meeting him, the sovereign people blessed me with the opportunity to serve as the Chief Minister of Gujarat. Since then until today, for the past 25 years, as the head of the government, I have been continuously serving the nation to the best of my ability; Guruji's blessings are with me. In this journey, the youth of the country stand at the centre of my efforts and policies. I am delighted that at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav as well, the youth have shouldered major responsibilities. Many of our young companions undertook a journey of 40,000 kilometres over nearly 300 days. During this period, more than one lakh youths were contacted. I congratulate the entire team for this remarkable endeavour as well.
Friends,
The declaration of our Upanishads is: “Vayam Amritasya Putrah”. That is, we are the children of immortality. This conception is not merely a spiritual philosophy; it is also our cultural conviction. This does not mean that our physical bodies are immortal; it means our consciousness is immortal. Our knowledge and our awareness are immortal. Because of this very awareness, this India has remained immortal for thousands of years. Because the very meaning of the word 'Bharat' is that which is engaged in the pursuit of knowledge and illumination.
Therefore, friends,
When the occasion of 75 years of the country's independence arrived, the thought came to my mind that we must not only turn this occasion into an inspirational platform for a developed India, but we must also revive that essence of India which knows how to live with immortal ideas, and which, through its experience of thousands of centuries, can care for humanity across eras. That is why I called for celebrating that occasion as the Amrit Mahotsav. And see, with the passage of time, one wondrous journey after another has continued to align with that resolution. Numerous spiritual, cultural, and social organisations took Amrit resolves at key milestones of their respective journeys during this period. And now, Chinmaya Mission is also joining the mission of India's Amrit Kaal in the form of its Amrit Mahotsav. And this indeed is the true strength of India's resolves; this is the genuine proof of our being “Amritasya Putrah”.
Friends,
The call of our Vedas is: "Vayam Rashtre Jagriyama Purohitah" - meaning, may we, who seek the welfare of the nation, keep the nation awakened and elevated. Swami Chinmayananda ji lived his entire life guided by this very mantra. With as much devotion as he spoke on spiritual matters, with equal promptness he delivered articulate discourses on national issues. Because our nation is the birthplace of our culture. This nation is the very foundation of our existence. Swamiji always taught that we should link our spiritual advancement with personal growth, and make personal growth the vehicle for national progress. To fill the people of India with self-respect towards India was Swamiji's mission. With this objective, he initiated the Gita Jnana Yajna. He began the campaign of taking the wisdom of the Upanishads, Vedanta, and our scriptures to the common people. And today, we can see the results of that resolution of his in many ways. Due to the efforts of Chinmaya Mission, today there are lakhs of youth who are serving as cultural brand ambassadors of India. These youth are passing on Indian values to the new generation. This contribution of Pujya Gurudev is an important chapter in India's cultural and spiritual renaissance.
Friends,
Today, I also recall the occasion of Pujya Gurudev's birth centenary. In 2015, I had the privilege of releasing a special commemorative coin in his memory. Even then, I had remarked that Swamiji's life was a wonderful confluence of knowledge, action, and devotion. His Guru, Swami Sivananda ji, had blessed him with the words: “Go, roar like a lion.” He lived his entire life in that very spirit. The confidence and inner strength in his speech left an enduring impression of his thoughts on everyone's heart. His radio programme named ‘Art of Man Making’ provided direction to countless individuals.
Friends,
The mission of great personalities remains alive even after they depart. That is why today we see that more than 100 educational institutions of Chinmaya Mission are shaping the future of lakhs of children and youth. In these institutions, they are receiving modern education while also assimilating Indian values.
Friends,
The vision that visionary individuals like Swami Chinmayananda ji held at the time of independence - today the nation is fulfilling its responsibilities in that very direction. To ensure that our education system aligns with the needs of a new India, we introduced the National Education Policy. In this new Education Policy, priority has been accorded to Indian knowledge traditions, education in the mother tongue, modern science, and new technology.
Friends,
Another mission of Swamiji's life was: pride in Indian heritage and its preservation! All of you are familiar with the Vivekananda Rock Memorial in Kanyakumari. The resolution to build a memorial on that massive rock amidst the sea was taken by Shri Eknath Ranade ji. At that time, Pujya Gurudev stood firmly by his side. The first financial contribution for this great endeavour was also made by Pujya Swamiji. Today, the Vivekananda Rock Memorial stands as a centre of inspiration for lakhs of people visiting from across the country and the world.
Friends,
Today, from north to south, east to west, India's cultural centres are undergoing a renaissance. Be it the renewed form of Kashi Vishwanath Dham, the grand temple of Lord Shri Ram in Ayodhya, the Mahakal Mahalok of Ujjain, or our shrines like Kedarnath and Badrinath. If you have visited Kedarnath ji recently, a divine, grand statue of Adi Shankar, Adi Shankaracharya ji, has been established there, where Adi Shankar shed his mortal coil. Today, they are returning to their majestic form. All of you know that at one time, so many statues were stolen from India, taken abroad, and sold there. There was no one to stop it, no one to inquire - leave aside those who worshipped them, there was no one even to ask. Over the past 12 years, we have brought back more than six hundred and fifty such stolen ancient statues. Our cultural centres are becoming part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Friends,
Just as Swamiji took our dharma and philosophy to the people of the world, similarly, today International Yoga Day is connecting people across the globe with India and with our ancient, glorious tradition. This confidence of taking pride in our heritage, this assurance of liberation from the mindset of subjugation, is evidence that the nation is now advancing on the path envisioned for centuries by our rishis and patriots. Their strength of thought is our greatest asset along this path.
Friends,
Different institutions and organisations have their respective objectives, but the one purpose that unites everyone, the destination where all paths converge, that goal is: the development of the nation, the pride of the nation. In Swami Chinmayananda ji's time, according to the challenges that lay before the country, he shaped his resolutions. In the passing decades, times have changed, new challenges have arisen before the nation, and new distortions have entered society. Today, the responsibility of finding solutions rests upon all of us. Today, we have to unite society against divisive forces, and make our fellow citizens aware of self-reliance. We have to connect every individual with the resolution of a Developed India by 2047. We must become even more proactive towards these objectives.
Friends,
In 2047, when India completes 100 years of its independence, around that very period, Chinmaya Mission will also celebrate its centenary year. That is to say, Chinmaya Mission's centenary journey and the journey towards a Developed India will progress together. Therefore, our goals are one, our objectives are one, and we must take this journey forward together. You possess the great legacy of Gurudev and decades of experience. You have a vast family of dedicated Acharyas, seekers, and workers across the globe. I am confident that all of you together will play an important role in building a Developed India. With this conviction, I once again bow at the feet of Pujya Gurudev. I extend my heartiest congratulations on the Amrit Mahotsav to all the saints, Acharyas, seekers, and service-oriented companions of Chinmaya Mission.
Hari Om.
Hari Om.
Hari Om.
Thank you very much.

content:
The ICAR–Central Institute for Research on Cotton Technology (ICAR-CIRCOT), Mumbai, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with M/s. Trust ARS Rubber Private Limited, Chengalpattu, on 22 October 2026, for the technology transfer of "Protective Gloves for Cotton Picking Workers."
This technology transfer is expected to facilitate commercialization and ensure wider availability of the gloves, directly benefiting cotton farmers and agricultural workers. By promoting the adoption of suitable protective equipment, the initiative aims to reduce hand injuries, improve working conditions, and foster safer harvesting practices, contributing significantly to the overall well-being of agricultural labourers.
The technology was developed to enhance the safety and protection of cotton-picking workers during harvesting operations. The specially designed gloves protect workers’ hands against injuries caused by sharp cotton bracts while ensuring flexibility and comfort. Additionally, their reusable and durable construction makes them well-suited for repeated use under demanding agricultural field conditions.
The collaboration marks an important step toward strengthening industry–research partnerships and translating ICAR-CIRCOT’s technological innovations into practical solutions for the agricultural sector. Through this partnership, ICAR-CIRCOT reaffirms its commitment to developing and transferring need-based technologies that address field-level challenges, enhance occupational safety, and improve livelihoods across the cotton value chain.

title: NAAS Showcases India’s Agricultural Excellence at World Food Prize Foundation Symposium 2026; Indian Student Wins Global Youth Institute Award
subtitle: Dr. M. L. Jat emphasizes global partnerships in agricultural higher education; NAAS-CAST MoU signed to strengthen international cooperation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Academy of Agricultural Sciences (NAAS), New Delhi, showcased India’s agricultural research excellence at the prestigious World Food Prize Foundation (WFPF) event entitled “2026 Norman E Borlaug International Dialogue” with a theme “Before Hunger Wins”, held from October 20-22, 2026, in Des Moines, Iowa, USA.
The Academy’s participation featured a dedicated exhibition booth showcasing prominent publications of NAAS and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), participation of young Indian students at the Global Youth Institute (GYI), a special roundtable on Agricultural Higher Education, and the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between NAAS and the Council for Agricultural Science and Technology (CAST), USA.
Seven high school students from different parts of India, selected through the NAAS-YUVA selection drive, participated in the GYI programme of WFPF, where they presented their global research papers addressing critical food-security challenges. Their participation provided an opportunity to engage with international peers and exchange perspectives on food security and sustainable agri-food systems. In a proud moment for the Academy,
Ms. Ameena Nazreen A S
won GYI Award of US$500 cash prize, bringing recognition to NAAS, India and showcasing the potential of India’s young talent on a prestigious global platform.
The NAAS exhibition booth attracted attention to India’s scientific contributions through a display of prominent publications of the Academy and ICAR. The initiative provided an international platform to share Indian agricultural research, scientific knowledge and policy perspectives with researchers, academicians, policymakers and other stakeholders.
Earlier, a special roundtable on “Agricultural Higher Education”, organised alongside the 2026 Norman E. Borlaug International Dialogue, brought the Indian agricultural diaspora into discussion on transforming agricultural education through global partnerships. Addressing the meeting virtually, Dr. M.L. Jat, President, NAAS, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), and Director General, ICAR, called for reimagining agricultural higher education to prepare future professionals to address global challenges, including climate change, natural resource degradation, biodiversity loss and the growing demand for nutritious and healthy food.
In his address, Dr. Jat emphasized the need to move beyond production-centric agriculture towards an integrated agri-food systems and value-chain approach. title: Department of Commerce and EEPC India Hold Chintan Shivir to Chart Strategy for US $250 Billion Engineering Exports by 2030

India’s Engineering Exports Cross US$70 Billion in First Half of FY 2026-27, Register Nearly 20% Growth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Commerce and EEPC India, the country's apex engineering exports promotion body, held multiple brainstorming sessions as part of the Chintan Shivir for the Engineering Sector to chart a strategy for achieving total engineering goods exports of US$250 billion by 2030, deepening market access through better utilisation of free trade pacts and enhancing the global competitiveness of the sector by securing the long-term availability of key raw materials.
The sessions brought together top policymakers, industry leaders, sector experts and concerned stakeholders.
The discussions highlighted concerns about the availability of quality raw materials at competitive prices and the need for a resilient, competitive supply chain to support the long-term growth of engineering exports. It was noted that volatility in input costs, supply-chain disruptions, global overcapacity and trade-protective measures can affect the competitiveness of Indian engineering exports.
In his keynote address, Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, highlighted the resilience of India’s exports amid global uncertainties.
India’s total exports of merchandise and services grew by 14% year-on-year to US$476.20 billion during April–September 2026–27. He also highlighted the potential to increase India’s share in global merchandise exports from approximately 2% to 15–20%, stressing the need to leverage the country’s competitive advantages.
During the first six months of FY 2026–27, engineering exports crossed US$70 billion, registering nearly 20% growth over the corresponding period of the previous year.”
Addressing emerging challenges, including Quality Control Orders (QCOs), sustainability-related trade measures and climate-linked requirements affecting market access, Shri Agrawal emphasised the need for ambitious export targets to drive growth and strengthen global competitiveness. He further stressed industry-wide collaboration to address common challenges and identify practical solutions, while encouraging stakeholders to adopt relevant global best practices to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem and enhance engineering export potential.
Addressing the gathering, Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Vimal Anand, underscored the promising export performance of the engineering sector and called upon EEPC India to revisit its ambition of achieving US $300 billion in engineering exports by 2030. He observed that, with sustained efforts and continued industry–government collaboration, engineering exports could potentially reach US $300 billion by 2030.
Shri Anand also emphasised the need for EEPC India to prepare a comprehensive white paper on QCOs applicable to the engineering sector, examining the sectors and products covered, the rationale for their introduction and their impact on industry. Such a study would facilitate a more nuanced, evidence-based understanding of the implications of QCOs for the engineering sector.
Further, he called upon EEPC India to actively seek feedback from members across all its engineering panels to ensure that the challenges and concerns of different segments of the sector are comprehensively captured and adequately represented in policy deliberations.
Chairman, EEPC India, Shri Pankaj Chadha, expressed confidence that India's engineering sector would continue to scale new heights through closer industry–government collaboration.
“We are very much on track to surpass export numbers of the previous financial year. Our medium- and long-term growth outlook remains positive. Engineering exports are expected to cross US$140 billion this current financial year,” he said.

title: Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) Establishes Sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE) At IIT (BHU), Varanasi to Advance Next-Generation Telecom Technologies

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:
The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier telecom R&D centre of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi, a leading institution of national importance, for establishing C-DOT’s sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE). The partnership brings together C-DOT, a market leader in indigenous telecommunications research and development with the academic and research strengths of IIT (BHU), Varanasi, to strengthen India’s telecom innovation ecosystem.
The collaboration between C-DOT and IIT (BHU) is aimed at bridging academic research with real-world technology requirements, creating opportunities for innovation while building a strong pipeline of skilled professionals for the evolving telecommunications sector. It will bring together researchers, faculty, students and technology experts from C-DOT and IIT (BHU) to undertake joint research and promote sustained knowledge exchange. The initiative will strengthen academia and industry to support development of native technologies in areas critical to nation’s digital and communication infrastructure.
CoE will focus in technologies such as Wireless Communications, Quantum Technologies, Cybersecurity and AI-driven Communication Systems. It will undertake advanced research in emerging areas including 5G Advanced/6G Technologies, very large-scale Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, Integrated Sensing and Communication, AI-Native Communication Networks and devices, and Quantum and Post-Quantum Communication Technologies.
The MoU was signed in the presence of Dr. Pankaj Kumar Dalela, EVP, C-DOT, and Professor Amit Patra, Director, IIT (BHU), Varanasi, along with faculty members from IIT (BHU) and senior officials from C-DOT. The signing ceremony was followed by the inauguration of the Centre of Excellence dedicated to advancing communication technologies through collaborative research and innovation.
Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT, highlighted the importance of the collaboration and said, “This Centre of Excellence is more than a research platform, it is an investment in India’s future technology capabilities. The next generation of communications will be shaped by advances in AI, quantum technologies, advanced wireless systems and intelligent networks. Through this CoE, C-DOT and IIT (BHU) are creating a collaborative ecosystem to explore these frontiers and accelerate the development of indigenous technologies for India’s digital future.”
Prof Amit Patra, Director, IIT (BHU), said, “The collaboration with C-DOT will provide a strong platform for translating academic research into impactful technological solutions. It will enable our students and researchers to engage with real-world challenges in telecommunications while contributing to India’s journey towards self-reliance in advanced communication technologies.”
The establishment of the CoE further expands C-DOT’s national network of Centres of Excellence to six, building on its existing collaborations with IIT Kanpur, IIT Gandhinagar, IIT Roorkee, IIT Hyderabad and IISc Bengaluru through FSID. Together, these Centres serve to contribute to the development of future-ready communication technologies, promote knowledge exchange and nurture specialised talent.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that despite growing significance of challenges across the air, maritime, space and cyber domains, land warfare and ground forces would remain indispensable. He called for an integrated approach to modern warfare, stressing that success would depend on multi-domain capabilities and seamless coordination in joint operations.
Raksha Mantri acknowledged the self-reliance efforts of the defence forces, stating that India’s growing defence manufacturing capabilities are a result of concerted efforts of all stakeholders. “Amidst the changing global landscape, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government is prioritising Aatmanirbharta in defence. He urged the Defence Forces to maintain their focus on self-reliance, effective implementation of reforms, improved manpower management, greater participation of women and an integrated approach to national security.

title: INDIAN NAVY TO HOST INDO-PACIFIC REGIONAL DIALOGUE 2026 TO EXPLORE SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND ACADEMIC COOPERATION
subtitle: Three-day conference in New Delhi from 03 to 05 Nov 2026 to bring together experts from 18 countries; deliberations to focus on academic networks, maritime science, ocean governance, climate resilience, and emerging technologies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 12:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Over a three-day period spanning 03, 04 and 05 Nov 2026, the Indian Navy will conduct the 2026 edition of the ‘Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue’ (IPRD-2026), which is its annual apex-level international outreach conference pitched at the strategic level, at
the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi.
Organised in close association with the
National Maritime Foundation (NMF)
, which is the Navy’s knowledge partner and principal organiser of the event, this year’s conference will be centred upon the theme
‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’.
Successive editions of this annual dialogue have examined a variety of dimensions of the seven deeply-interconnected maritime lines-of-thrust of the
‘Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative’ (IPOI), which had been promulgated by India’s Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi,
at the 14th East Asia Summit (EAS) in Bangkok in Nov of 2019.  Importantly, the IPOI provides first-order specificity to India’s maritime vision of
MAHASAGAR
— Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.
Each edition of the IPRD seeks to provide second- and third-order specificity to the country’s maritime policy by translating the IPOI’s broad framework for cooperation into specific, actionable proposals.
The choice of this year’s theme reflects a fundamental feature of the contemporary maritime domain: the oceans are interconnected, but the scientific knowledge, technological capabilities and institutions required to understand and manage them remain unevenly distributed.  Care is being taken to ensure that the word ‘science’ is not allowed to be restricted to the ‘physical’ sciences alone, (which have traditionally encompassed ‘engineering’ and ‘technology’ — the latter being ‘applied engineering’) but also incorporate the ‘life sciences’, as also the ‘social sciences’.  Thus, the multifarious facets of climate change, maritime trade, the maritime ramifications of supply- and value-chains and their vulnerabilities, the ever-increasing pressure upon marine resources, and the growing threats to critical maritime infrastructure, will all form important elements of the conference.  Given that all these elements transcend national boundaries, effective responses require not merely more sophisticated technologies but stronger arrangements for cooperation, information-sharing, and the development of human capital.
The three days of this year’s conference will incorporate
five professional thematic sessions.
These professional sessions will address ‘Academic Networks, Research, and Human Capital Development’; ‘Maritime Situational Awareness and Protection of Critical Maritime Infrastructure’; ‘Oceanographic Science and Climate Resilience’; ‘Collaborative Approaches to Ocean Governance and Maritime Resilience’; and ‘Transformative Maritime Technologies and Dual-Use Implications’.  The deliberations will consider practical pathways for joint research, collaborative technology development, responsible governance, appropriate access to scientific data, and stronger institutional partnerships.
IPRD-2026 will also feature two ‘special’ sessions.  The first of these, entitled, ‘Perspectives from the Flag Bridge’, will bring together
former naval chiefs from India and Sri Lanka,
to offer experience-rich perspectives on the manner in which the enormous potential of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) could best be leveraged so as to promote cooperation in science, technology, and meaningful academic engagement across the western segment of the Indo-Pacific — the Indian Ocean.  The second is a special ambassadorial interaction entitled
‘Sahyog Ka Samvaad’.  ‘Sahyog’
is the Hindi word for ‘cooperation’, while
‘Samvaad’
is the Hindi word for ‘dialogue’.
The second day of the conference will, in addition to two professional sessions, also feature two ministerial sessions.  In the first one,
Shri Rajnath Singh, the Hon’ble Raksha Mantri (Defence Minister) of India, will deliver the Commemorative Address.
The second ministerial session will feature a
special address by Dr Jitendra Singh, the Hon’ble Minister of State (with independent charge) of the Government of India’s Ministry of Science and Technology.
IPRD-2026 will offer an intellectual spectacle of rare delight, with contributions from
maritime practitioners, scientists, academicians, policymakers and experts from 18 countries across the Indo-Pacific.
This edition of the IPRD has laid very considerable emphasis upon solution-oriented dialogue. Thus, the deliberations of this international conference will concentrate upon the identification of specific, actionable measures at national, sub-regional, and pan-regional levels, which would, thereafter, be addressed in greater granularity through extant mechanisms for bilateral, trilateral, and plurilateral engagement designed to promote comity, cooperation, and collaboration, across the Indo-Pacific.

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India

The new facility aims to strengthen the state’s IT/ITeS ecosystem by providing modern infrastructure to technology companies and startups, while fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, product development and employment generation.

30,000 sq. ft. across four floors,
the new incubation facility offers semi-furnished office spaces, high-speed internet connectivity, an air-conditioned and eco-friendly working environment, an auditorium, two meeting rooms, two conference rooms and a Network Operations Centre (NOC). The facility has been designed to provide a conducive working environment for technology enterprises, enabling collaboration, business development and growth.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Jitin Prasada, Hon’ble Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, said, “India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation is driven by two key engines: technology and trade. In an increasingly interconnected world, technological self-reliance is essential to ensure that the country is not dependent on external sources for critical technologies such as semiconductors. The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated how chip shortages can disrupt entire industries, underscoring the importance of building domestic manufacturing capabilities. Our focus on strengthening the semiconductor and electronics manufacturing ecosystem is aimed at securing India’s technological future while continuing to engage with the world and adopt global best practices.”
He further added, “STPI’s new incubation facility in Dehradun will provide a vibrant environment where startups and technology enterprises can collaborate, exchange ideas and develop innovative solutions. With Uttarakhand already having more than 1700 recognised startups, such initiatives can further strengthen the state’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. Alongside efforts to promote electronics manufacturing, including component manufacturing and the development of an Electronics Manufacturing Cluster in Kashipur, this facility will help attract investment, generate employment and create opportunities for young talent. Our aim is to build a self-reliant India that is equipped to compete globally and contributes meaningfully to the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Shri Pradeep Batra, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister of IT & Good Governance, Government of Uttarakhand, said, “The vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 goes beyond infrastructure development; it requires a transformation in our thinking, our aspirations and our commitment to the nation. Uttarakhand, our Devbhoomi, has immense potential to progress further, supported by the capabilities and dedication of its people. As the state attracts growing interest from tourists and businesses, strengthening infrastructure and improving access to modern facilities will be essential to meeting these aspirations. Initiatives such as STPI’s new incubation facility in Dehradun will help create an enabling environment for technology, innovation and entrepreneurship, contributing to Uttarakhand’s growth and India’s larger vision of a developed nation.”
Shri Ganesh Joshi, Hon’ble Agriculture Minister, Government of Uttarakhand, said, “Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat, we must create opportunities for our youth beyond the traditional IT hubs. Dehradun, already recognised as an education hub, has the potential to emerge as a prominent IT destination like Bengaluru and Hyderabad. I am confident that this new centre will open up new avenues for growth, strengthen Uttarakhand’s technology ecosystem and create greater opportunities for young people over the next five years.”
Shri Pankaj Pandey, IT Secretary, Government of Uttarakhand, said, “The new STPI incubation facility is a major addition to Uttarakhand’s technology ecosystem, offering young entrepreneurs the infrastructure and support including initiatives like the Centre of Entrepreneurship to convert their expertise into successful businesses. Alongside this entrepreneurial push, Uttarakhand is advancing digital governance by offering around 1,000 services online. The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), an autonomous scientific society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and Bank of India (BOI), signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on quantum financial innovation and the adoption of emerging technologies in banking on 22 October 2026.

The collaboration brings together C-DAC’s capabilities in High Performance Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Technologies, Blockchain, Cybersecurity and indigenous technology development with Bank of India’s banking domain expertise, nationwide presence and high-volume technology environment.
A key focus of the partnership will be the development of a
Quantum Ecosystem for Financial Innovation
, aimed at preparing banking systems for the opportunities as well as emerging security challenges associated with quantum technologies. The two organizations will jointly explore quantum-inspired and quantum-safe technologies that can strengthen security, trust, resilience and decision-making in banking.
The collaboration will seek to identify a prioritized portfolio of banking use cases, demonstrate Proofs of Concept in secure sandbox environments, assess technical feasibility and potential banking value, benchmark emerging approaches against existing systems, and develop roadmaps for further development, pilots or adoption.
Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary IAS, MeitY, congratulated Bank of India for its contribution to technological advancement and appreciated its collaboration with C-DAC to foster indigenous innovation. He emphasised the need to build a
quantum-resilient financial ecosystem
in an era of growing cybersecurity concerns and emerging technological threats, preparing the banking sector for the challenges and opportunities of the quantum era.

Magesh, Director General, C-DAC, said, This collaboration with Bank of India is an important step towards translating India’s indigenous quantum and emerging technology capabilities into practical banking solutions. Through joint research and development and capacity building, C-DAC aims to support a secure, resilient and future-ready financial ecosystem.

Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technologies relevant to financial services

The partnership will also focus on developing a future-ready talent ecosystem through training and capacity-building programmes in areas including Quantum Computing, Quantum Security, Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain and other emerging digital technologies.
The MoU was formally exchanged by Shri Aditya Kumar Sinha, Executive Director, C-DAC Mumbai and Shri Satyendra Singh , CGM IT & CIO, Bank of India , in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, IAS, Secretary, MeitY; Shri Rajiv Mishra, Executive Director, Bank of India, Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, Joint Secretary, MeitY, Shri E. Magesh Director General C-DAC, along with other senior officials from MeitY, Bank of India and C-DAC.

title: DRI seizes 5.6 kg of heroin in Phagwara, Punjab; Four drug traffickers arrested in intelligence-led operation

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in continuation to its crackdown on narcotics trafficking has seized 5.6 kg heroin, and arrested four persons in an intelligence-led operation conducted on 21st October 2026 in Phagwara, near Jalandhar, Punjab.
Acting on specific intelligence regarding the movement of narcotic drugs by some individuals travelling on a public transport bus, officers of DRI mounted a surveillance in the Phagwara area and intercepted a bus and four suspected individuals travelling as passengers were identified by the DRI team.
A personal search conducted in accordance with the provision of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, led to the recovery of five packets wrapped in yellow adhesive tape, concealed in a backpack kept on the lap of one of the suspects. Each of the five packets contained two smaller packets, making a total of ten packets. Field testing of the substance in all ten packets yielded positive results for Heroin, also commonly known as
Chitta
in Punjab. The total of 5.6 kg contraband was recovered, and was seized under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and all four persons allegedly involved in the transportation and possession of the contraband were arrested under the Act.
Heroin is a highly addictive opioid that depresses the central nervous system and carries a serious risk of dependence, respiratory depression, overdose and death. In India, it is a prohibited narcotic drug regulated under the NDPS Act, 1985. Unauthorised possession, trafficking, transport or sale attracts stringent penalties; for a commercial quantity, Section 21(c) prescribes rigorous imprisonment of 10–20 years and a fine of Rs. 1–2 lakh, with provision for a higher fine.
This significant seizure in Punjab underscores DRI’s sustained efforts to disrupt narcotics supply chains, and bring those involved in the trafficking of illicit narcotics to justice.

title: DRI busts another attempt to circumvent ban on Pakistani goods under ‘operation deep manifest’; seizes around 25,000 kg Pakistan-origin watermelon seeds; two arrested
subtitle: Investigation uncovers Dubai-routed transshipment and misdeclaration of country of origin; Detection of total 46,920 kg Pakistani origin watermelon and muskmelon seeds smuggled into the country
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), under
Operation Deep Manifest
, has unearthed another attempt to circumvent India’s prohibition on the import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan. The operation, conducted between 11 September and 22 October 2026, led to the interception of a consignment of around
25,000 kg Pakistan-origin watermelon seeds
that had been routed through Dubai and falsely declared as of UAE origin to evade the import prohibition. Two persons were arrested on 22nd October 2026.
Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers examined a consignment of around 25,000 kg seeds, declared as of UAE-origin muskmelon seeds, imported through Nhava Sheva Port. Although, examination revealed that the goods were watermelon seeds, with evidence indicating their Pakistani origin.
Preliminary investigation revealed a deliberate transshipment arrangement designed to conceal the true origin of the goods. The seeds were initially shipped from Karachi Port, Pakistan, to Jebel Ali Port, Dubai, in one set of containers aboard a vessel. Following transshipment at Jebel Ali, the goods were transferred into another set of containers and loaded onto a different vessel for onward shipment to India. The change of containers and vessels, coupled with the misdeclaration of country of origin and fabricated import documentation, was intended to disguise the Pakistani origin of the consignment. The investigations yielded crucial documentary evidence, clearly establishing the movement of the consignment from Pakistan through Dubai to India, contradicting the declared UAE origin.
The investigation further revealed that the import was in contravention of the applicable import policy on two counts. First, the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan is prohibited under DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025. Second, watermelon seeds have been restricted for import into India with effect from 1 July 2024, vide DGFT Notification No. 02/2023 dated 5 April 2024. Accordingly, the consignment, having a market value of approximately Rs. 2.02 crore, was seized on 14 October 2026 under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
Further investigation revealed that the importer had brought in an earlier consignment of
22,000 kg muskmelon seeds
in February 2026 from the same Dubai-based supplier, declaring the goods as UAE-origin.  The evidences indicates that this consignment had also been transshipped, thus casting serious doubt on the declared country of origin.
Investigation has revealed the involvement of two related persons, the son and nephew of the Importer Exporter Code (IEC) holder, who were allegedly handling different legs of the operation. The son is the owner and director of the Dubai-based supplier firm, while his cousin was handling import-related formalities and domestic sales in India. Both persons were arrested on 22 October 2026.
This operation follows DRI’s recent major enforcement actions against Pakistani-origin goods routed through third countries to evade India’s import prohibition. In September 2026, DRI seized over 362 metric tonnes of Pakistani-origin dry dates packed in 13 containers at CFS Ambad, Nashik, after uncovering their transshipment through Jebel Ali, Dubai, and misdeclaration of origin. More recently, in Oct.2026, DRI detected an illegal import of 295 containers carrying 7,311 metric tonnes of Pakistani-origin industrial/Himalayan rock salt routed through Colombo, Sri Lanka, using fabricated certificates of origin and invoices.
Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, the Government of India prohibited the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, in the interest of national security and public policy, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025.
DRI remains committed to identifying and dismantling networks engaged in customs fraud and the circumvention of import prohibitions, thereby safeguarding the integrity of India’s trade controls and economic security.

The FSDC, inter alia, deliberated on issues related to macro financial stability and India’s preparedness to deal with them. Considering the importance of regulatory improvisation and digital modernization in the financial sector, the FSDC discussed measures towards promoting innovation in the Fintech sector and exploring the prospects of tokenisation of financial assets and other real-world assets.
The Council reviewed the cyber resilience of the Indian financial sector and took note of the Financial Sector Cyber Security Strategy (FSCSS) formulated by an Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG) comprising of financial sector regulators and cybersecurity agencies, in coordination with the DEA, DFS and MeitY. The implementation of the FSCSS is expected to strengthen the overall resilience of the Indian financial sector. The discussions also covered India’s preparedness to protect the Critical Information Infrastructure and resilience of protection systems and improving cybersecurity preparedness of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs).
The FSDC also discussed issues relating to formulating a strategy for implementing the past decisions and the budget announcements, which included:
strengthening the domestic investment ecosystem and improve resource flow for investment including in the GIFT-IFSC;
simplification and digitalization of the KYC processes and digital onboarding for NRIs and FPIs;
reforms to scale up DPIs in India including the Account Aggregator and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) framework with specific focus on MSMEs;
reducing cost of intermediation in the financial sector, improving the responsiveness of regulations and rationalization of Credit Guarantee Schemes in India.
The FSDC took cognizance of the emerging trends from domestic and global macro-financial situation and stressed upon the need to be vigilant especially in view of the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, AI boom and steep rise in global bond yields. The Council recognised the need for proactive efforts to mitigate potential risks to financial stability while adopting adequate safeguards for financial system’s resilience. The members decided to strengthen the inter-regulatory coordination for wider development of the financial sector.
The Union Finance Minister also urged the regulators and stakeholders concerned to expedite the process of refund of unclaimed assets (banks deposits, dividends, shares, post office accounts, insurance and pension funds etc.) to their rightful owners.
The FSDC noted the success undertaken by stakeholders under “Your Money, Your Right” campaign at the district level to refund the existing unclaimed financial assets and guided Ministries and Regulators to pursue additional efforts for timely refund to rightful owners.
Given rising geopolitical headwinds and global uncertainty, Smt. Sitharaman urged the Council to hold FSDC meetings at more frequent intervals with a predefined schedule.
The FSDC also took note of the activities undertaken by the FSDC Sub-Committee chaired by the Governor, RBI, and the action taken on the pending past decisions of the FSDC.

title: India moves to development phase of national action plan for inland small-scale fisheries
subtitle: India sets target of 30 million tonnes in fish production in next 5 years, says Union Fisheries Secretary
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India has moved into the development phase of a separate national action plan for inland small-scale fisheries, with a focus on livelihood improvement, enhanced coordination and better management of freshwater resources.Dr Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India  on Friday formally launched India’s development phase of the National Plan of Action (NPOA) for small-scale inland fisheries. The plan is being developed under the framework of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's (FAO). The initiative is being led by the Union Department of Fisheries in collaboration with the Bay of Bengal Programme Inter-Governmental Organisation (BOBP-IGO).
A two-day national workshop in Bhopal identified key priorities for developing the action plan, including a proposed programme of consultations with fishing communities and other stakeholders. Experts from fisheries institutions and stakeholders prepared a framework for the activities to be undertaken in the development phase.  Addressing the gathering, Dr Abhilaksh Likhi called for a mission-mode outreach programme to take India's proposed national action plan for sustainable inland small-scale fisheries to fishing communities across the country. “The document must translate into practical improvements in livelihoods rather than remain confined to government offices”, he said, adding that the proposed plan must prioritise sustainability amid climate crisis, and strengthen value chains to improve fishers’ income.
*
30 million tonnes fish production in next 5 years*
Dr Likhi further said: “India has set a target of 30 million tonnes in fish production over the next five years, while seafood exports are expected to rise to Rs 1.25 lakh crore”. Highlighting the sector's current status, he said India had achieved an annual fish production of 19.7 million tonnes, with inland fisheries contributing approximately three-fourths of this output, while seafood exports had crossed Rs 70,000 crore.. However, Fisheries Secretary stressed that production and export growth must go hand in hand with securing the livelihoods of small-scale fishers.On sustainability, Dr Likhi flagged climate change and deteriorating water quality as major concerns for inland fisheries, pointing to challenges such as declining oxygen levels in water bodies. He said the plan must incorporate measures to build climate resilience, drawing on the experience of fishing communities who directly confront these challenges.
Diversity
“India's diverse inland fisheries sector, with its varied ecosystems, fishing communities and region-specific challenges, could serve as a model for the FAO to collaborate, pilot region-specific approaches and take the learnings to wider geographies.  The experiences of fishing communities across the country could help shape context-specific approaches to sustainable fisheries management and livelihood development, offering valuable lessons for wider application”, Secretary Likhi added. The proposed plan covers fisheries in rivers, canals, reservoirs, lakes, floodplain wetlands, tanks and cold-water systems.
“The development phase is expected to address issues relating to fishing rights and resource management, employment and decent work, gender equality, value chains and post-harvest trade, as well as disaster risks and climate change”, said Dr P Krishnan, Director of BOBP-IGO. The plan will be finalised through stakeholder consultations before its public launch next month and subsequent implementation.
Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Secretary Swantantra Kumar Singh, Joint Secretary  Dr Gunjan Krishna and FAO Project Officer Giulia Gorelli also spoke on the occasion.
