The Department of Fisheries, Government of Madhya Pradesh, in association with the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying (MoFAHD), Government of India (GoI) & NFDB, organised the
Fisheries Investors & Exporters Conclave 2026
in Bhopal on 23 October 2026 to strengthen investment, processing, value addition and export opportunities in inland fisheries.
The Conclave was graced by Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj; and Shri Narayan Singh Pawar, Hon’ble Minister, Department of Fishermen Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh, Dr Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India, Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh,
Shri Ashok Barnwal
. Investors, exporters, fish farmers, entrepreneurs from India and abroad along with senior officials of the Central and State Governments and other stakeholders across the fisheries value chain, were also present.
The Conclave brought together investors, exporters, fishers, more than 1,000 fish farmers from across Madhya Pradesh, fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs), entrepreneurs, start-ups, processors, financial institutions, research organisations and other stakeholders across the fisheries value chain.
India's fish production reached 197.75 lakh MT in 2024–25, of which inland fisheries contributed 151.60 lakh tonnes, accounting for nearly three-fourths of the country's total fish production. India's seafood exports were valued at ₹73,890 crore in 2025–26. The Conclave focused on connecting this production base with processing, cold-chain infrastructure, quality assurance, market access and exports.
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India, and Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, released the Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Investment and Export Guidelines, 2026, and the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) of Inland State Export Potential. These aim to facilitate investment across hatcheries, fish seed and feed, reservoir and cage fisheries, aquatic animal health, processing, cold-chain infrastructure, logistics, value addition and market development. Madhya Pradesh has been notified by the Central Government as a Reservoir Fisheries Cluster.
The programme also featured the virtual inauguration of integrated cage culture units and the handover of administrative approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in Madhya Pradesh.
Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh handed over the Administrative Approval for the Integrated Development of Reservoirs in Madhya Pradesh, under the Union Budget Announcement 2026–27, to the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh. The initiative envisages the development of 49 reservoirs in the State at an approved project cost of ₹8755.60 Lakh, and 5 Amrit Sarovar at an approved project cost of ₹69 Lakhs.
The initiative aims to harness the fisheries potential of reservoirs, enhance fish production and productivity, strengthen infrastructure, generate livelihood and employment opportunities, and improve the socio-economic well-being of fishers and fish farmers in the state.
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India, and Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, distributed certificates to beneficiaries under various fisheries-related initiatives, including the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) for fisheries, fisheries cooperatives, fisheries start-ups and the Performance Grant under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY).
Dr. Mohan Yadav, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh
,
highlighted the fisheries sector’s growing potential as a driver of investment, entrepreneurship, industrial development and exports, noting the increasing participation of investors, exporters, entrepreneurs and start-ups. Emphasising water resource management, he stated that the State’s irrigation potential had increased to 60 lakh hectares over the past two and a half years, with a target of 100 lakh hectares by the end of the State Government’s tenure. He highlighted the Ken–Betwa and Parvati–Kalisindh–Chambal river-linking projects, alongside efforts to develop reservoirs and conserve traditional water bodies, to strengthen water availability and create opportunities for fisheries.
Announcing
three key initiatives,
he outlined the integration of fisheries with the food processing industry to promote processing, value addition, packaging, cold-chain infrastructure and distribution; support and incentives for fisheries enterprises under the MSME framework, including land and other facilities; and the launch of the Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Policy 2026, providing for land allocation and facilities for fisheries enterprises. These measures aim to attract investment, generate employment and unlock the State’s fisheries and aquaculture potential.
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India,
noted that India exports fish to 130 countries, but inland states contribute only 2% of total fisheries exports, despite a 147% increase in fish production in these states. He emphasised the need to develop reservoirs and large ponds through scientific cage and pen culture, improve productivity and connect fish farmers with investors, processors and exporters. Welcoming the Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Investment and Export Promotion Policy 2026, he stressed that fisheries must be recognised and developed as an industry to attract investment, generate employment and enhance incomes.
He underscored the importance of quality fish production, efficient logistics, value addition, ready-to-cook products and reliable supply chains to meet international market demand. Highlighting traceability as essential for export competitiveness, he referred to the National Framework for Aquaculture Traceability 2025 and the National Fisheries Digital Platform, which support digital documentation across the aquaculture value chain. He also noted that MPEDA would support inland-state exporters with market intelligence.
Outlining five priorities for export promotion,
the Union Minister called for identifying export-suitable freshwater fish species and target markets; developing fish collection centres and large-scale processing hubs; strengthening partnerships among farmers, cooperatives, investors and exporters; ensuring quality certification and traceability from the outset; and maintaining continuous engagement with international buyers and clear export targets.
He further urged stakeholders to follow the SOP released at the conclave, which provides guidance across the value chain, from fish seed stocking and production to export requirements. He called upon the State Government and industry stakeholders to work in a coordinated manner to position Madhya Pradesh as a leading contributor to India’s inland fisheries exports.
Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, GoI
emphasising Madhya Pradesh’s vast inland fisheries potential, noted that the State’s extensive river network, reservoirs and favourable water quality provide significant opportunities for fisheries development. He highlighted the potential of Indira Sagar Reservoir for large-scale cage culture, noting that the development of one lakh cages could set a unique example for the country.
The Minister observed that the creation of an independent Department of Fisheries in 2019 had accelerated the sector’s growth and strengthened its development vision. He emphasised that inland fisheries, which account for approximately 75% of India’s fish production, offer substantial opportunities for investment, exports and livelihood generation. He underlined the important role of inland states, particularly Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar and Chhattisgarh, in driving the next phase of fisheries sector growth.
Shri Narayan Singh Panwar, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Department of Fishermen Welfare and Fisheries Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh,
highlighted the State Government’s efforts to transform fisheries from a livelihood activity into a growth-oriented sector driven by modern technology, investment,
entrepreneurship, employment and higher incomes. In this direction, the Integrated Fisheries Industry Policy 2026 has been launched to enhance fish production through better utilisation of water resources and large-scale promotion of modern cage culture in suitable districts.
Emphasising the importance of translating investment and technology into local benefits, he noted that increased production would enhance incomes and create employment opportunities for fisher families. With the support of the Government of India, the Sardar Sarovar, Indira Sagar and Vindhyavasini clusters are being developed, with efforts to replicate successful models across other districts and establish an integrated system from production to market.
He further stated that the Department would act as a facilitator and partner, connecting investors, fish farmers and fishing communities to enable viable investments at the grassroots level. Inviting investors and entrepreneurs to participate in Madhya Pradesh’s inland blue economy, the speaker reaffirmed the State’s commitment to increasing production, attracting investment, generating employment and ensuring the prosperity of fisher families.
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India,
highlighted the untapped export potential of inland fisheries. He noted that freshwater species such as Pangasius and Tilapia currently account for only 2% of seafood exports, with a target to increase their share to 10% over the next five years. States such as Madhya Pradesh can play a key role by utilising reservoirs, ponds, lakes and rivers, alongside investments in infrastructure, cold chains, certification and export market access.
Dr Likhi further highlighted the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for cargo handling, prepared by the Government of India with MPEDA’s support, to facilitate inland fish exports. The Madhya Pradesh Fisheries Investment and Business Promotion Policy 2026 was also noted as an important initiative. Over the next five years, a cluster-based approach under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), in collaboration with State Governments, will support training, value addition, packaging, branding and export logistics for inland fish and seafood, he added.
Shri Ashok Barnwal, Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh,
highlighted the State’s ambitious plan to increase fish production from 4.5 lakh tonnes to 10–11 lakh tonnes over the next two to three years through the adoption of modern fisheries technologies under the Blue Revolution.
He stated that the proposed expansion could generate an estimated ₹5,000 crore in additional annual income for the fisheries sector, benefiting at least 50,000 people. Emphasising the sector’s transformation from a supplementary livelihood activity into a driver of investment and full-time employment, he invited investors and industry stakeholders to partner with Madhya Pradesh in developing fisheries exports, processing and backward linkages.
The Conclave highlighted the need to move beyond a production-oriented approach towards integrated fisheries value chains that connect production with processing, value addition, branding and markets. Stronger cold-chain connectivity, quality standards, certification and logistics can help inland fish products reach wider domestic and international markets.
The discussions and initiatives are expected to strengthen collaboration among Central and State Governments, investors, exporters, financial institutions, research organisations, fisheries cooperatives and entrepreneurs, translating Madhya Pradesh's inland fisheries potential into investment opportunities, stronger value chains and improved livelihood opportunities for fishers and fish farmers.
Background Note
Madhya Pradesh has 4.50 lakh hectares of inland water area, including 3.75 lakh hectares of reservoirs, providing a substantial production base for inland fisheries and aquaculture. Major species produced in the State are Rohu, Catla, Mrigal, Tilapia, Pangasius, Common Carp and Grass Carp.
Under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has accorded approvals to Madhya Pradesh at a total project cost of ₹910.81 crore, with a Central share of ₹305.50 crore, and released ₹301.27 crore, equivalent to about 98.61per cent of the approved Central share. As a result, fish production in Madhya Pradesh increased from 2.00 lakh MT in 2019-20 to 4.45 lakh MT in 2024-25, registering an increase of about 123 per cent.
The major production-related interventions approved under PMMSY include 78 hatcheries, 1,157 RAS and biofloc units, expansion of pond area by more than 5,700 hectares and one Integrated Aquapark.
Under the Budget Announcement 2026-27, integrated development of 49 reservoirs and 5 Amrit Sarovars are approved to Madhya Pradesh with an investment of Rs. ₹88.25 crore. Madhya Pradesh has established 316 cages in Halali Reservoir notified as a Reservoir Fisheries cluster. The Integrated Cage Culture units being inaugurated during this programme will further support planned production and marketing of fish.
Under FIDF, five projects have been approved in Madhya Pradesh:(i) fisheries training centre at a cost of ₹5.00 crore, (ii) cold storage at a cost of ₹1.21 crore, (iii) two innovative Projects at a cost of ₹0.44 crore and (iv) Establishment of Disease Diagnostic lab at a cost of ₹ 0.27crore. so far out of 5 projects 1 project related to fisheries training centre is ongoing while 4 yet to start.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Healthcare Services and Infrastructure Development at ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital

ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital Record Over 19 Lakh OPD Visits in 2025, Strengthen Quality Standards and Patient Care

content:
Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda reviewed the progress of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) and Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital (Dr. RML Hospital), New Delhi, focusing on patient care, specialised services, service delivery and infrastructure development. During the visit, he reviewed the hospital’s achievements and upcoming projects.
Through a presentation shared during the review meeting, the Minister was briefed on the hospital’s clinical services, medical education, research activities and quality improvement initiatives. The presentation highlighted the hospital’s growing patient load, with 19.4 lakh outpatient visits, over 82,500 inpatient admissions and more than 96,600 surgeries and procedures recorded in 2025. The hospital currently has 30 clinical and patient-care departments and eight pre-clinical and para-clinical departments.
The hospital’s achievement of full National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) accreditation in 2025 was highlighted during the presentation. Dr. RML Hospital became the first Central Government multi-specialty hospital to achieve this distinction. Quality improvement measures at the hospital include strengthening registration and triage processes, clinical and prescription audits, incident reporting, adverse drug reaction reporting and patient feedback mechanisms.
Prioritising better access to services, the hospital has also expanded the number of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) kiosks from one to three. The number of PM-JAY pre-authorisation requests rose from 549 in 2022 to 1,516 in 2025.
The presentation also featured the institute’s academic and research contributions, including over 2,200 research publications. Its roadmap for Viksit Bharat 2047 envisages digital, patient-centric care, stronger specialised services, expanded community outreach through satellite clinics and AI-enabled monitoring, and environmentally sustainable healthcare infrastructure.
Addressing the review meeting, Shri J.P. Nadda emphasised the importance of drawing on the expertise and best practices of leading institutions when planning major healthcare infrastructure projects. He also called for stronger implementation of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) at Dr. RML Hospital, including ABDM compliance and wider adoption of e-prescriptions and other digital health services to improve patient care and service delivery.
The Minister also stressed the need to prioritise the mental well-being of students and faculty, highlighting the impact of stress on academic and professional life. He called for supportive interpersonal relationships, open communication and sustained mental health support. RML Hospital regularly conducts mental health screenings for students and health check-ups for faculty members. Furthermore, the Minister encouraged the implementation of Project SARATHI at the institution and deemed it as an important step.
The Minister also reviewed the activities undertaken by Dr. RML Hospital under Special Campaign 6, emphasising the importance of institutionalising Swachhata, minimising pendency, ensuring efficient record management and maintaining a clean, hygienic and patient-friendly healthcare environment.
The review meeting was also attended by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare; Shri L.G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS); Smt. G. S. Chitra, Joint Secretary (Health); Dr. Akhilandeswari Prasad, Director, ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital; Dr. (Prof.) Vivek Dewan, Medical Superintendent, Dr. RML Hospital and other officials and faculty members of the institute and hospital.

title: In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the work to establish a vibrant Civil Defence Network in the country is set to begin
subtitle:
Three-day specialized training for Civil Defence Master Trainers to be conducted in 12 States/UTs in the first phase

In 1st phase, 600 Civil Defence Master Trainers, 50 from each participating State/UT, are proposed to be trained by the second week of November 2026

Following the specialized training, each Master Trainer will impart further training to 100 Civil Defence Volunteers in their respective State/UT

The initiative seeks to enhance the preparedness of Civil Defence personnel to respond effectively to emergencies

The training will cover three broad areas: Threat Awareness, Protection and Emergency Response and Communication and Coordination

A key feature of the initiative is its multiplier effect through a structured Master Trainer Model

Initiative marks a significant step towards combining the Indian Army’s operational expertise with the Civil Defence volunteer network
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India to build a vibrant Civil Defence Network with first-of-its-kind Joint Training Initiative with the Indian Army. A three-day specialized training for Civil Defence Master Trainers to be conducted in 12 States/UTs in the first phase.
In his address to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on 15 August 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced the vision of building a
vibrant Civil Defence network
, equipped with modern systems, technologies and contemporary preparedness capabilities to address emerging security challenges. In furtherance of this vision, the Directorate General of Fire Services, Civil Defence & Home Guards (DGFSCDHG), Ministry of Home Affairs, in coordination with the Indian Army, is undertaking a first-of-its-kind pilot initiative to strengthen Civil Defence preparedness through specialised training of Civil Defence Master Trainers by Indian Army.
In the first phase, a total of 600 Civil Defence Master Trainers, with 50 from each participating State/UT, are proposed to be trained by the second week of November 2026 through a three-day specialised training programme at designated Indian Army training establishments. The participating States/UTs are Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Delhi, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
The initiative seeks to enhance the preparedness of Civil Defence personnel to respond effectively to contemporary security threats, hostile situations and emergencies. The training will cover three broad areas:
Threat Awareness:
Modern and hybrid warfare, drone awareness and air-raid threats.
Protection and Emergency Response:
Critical infrastructure protection, fire safety, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) awareness, casualty management, search and rescue.
Communication and Coordination:
Emergency communication, cyber hygiene, digital resilience, civil-military coordination and incident command.
A key feature of the initiative is
its multiplier effect through a structured Master Trainer model
. Following the specialised training, each Master Trainer will impart further training to 100 Civil Defence Volunteers in their respective State/UT. This cascading mechanism has the potential to extend specialised preparedness skills to
60,000 Civil Defence Volunteers
across the 12 participating States/UTs, thereby significantly expanding the reach and impact of the initiative.
The initiative marks a significant step towards strengthening civil-military coordination and institutional preparedness by combining the Indian Army’s operational expertise with the Civil Defence volunteer network. It will enhance preparedness for emerging threats, coordinated emergency response and critical infrastructure protection. Based on the outcomes of the pilot phase, the initiative is envisaged to be expanded to the remaining States/UTs in a phased manner, furthering the Prime Minister Modi’s vision of a robust, responsive and future-ready Vibrant Civil Defence network.

title: 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition 2026 inaugurated in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
subtitle:
Union Minister of State Shri Tokhan Sahu inaugurates two-day Conference in the presence of Odisha Minister Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra

Conference focuses on ‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’

28 exhibitors showcase best practices, innovative technologies and solutions in urban transport

Day-one deliberations focused on digital mobility, intelligent transport, gender-responsive planning and sustainable urban transport
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 was inaugurated by Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu, in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, today. The two-day Conference, being held on 23–24 October 2026 at Hotel Mayfair Sanctuary, is being organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, through the Institute of Urban Transport (India), with the support of the Government of Odisha.
The inaugural session was attended by Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Government of Odisha; Smt. Anu Garg, Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha; Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA; and Smt. Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha. Senior officials from Central and State Governments, national and international experts, policymakers, representatives of Metro Rail Companies, transport undertakings, industry professionals and academicians also participated in the Conference.
The Conference is being organised under the theme
‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’
. It focuses on improving urban accessibility, integrated transport infrastructure and quality of urban life through emerging digital technologies. The deliberations cover sustainable and low-carbon public transport, seamless multimodal integration, first- and last-mile connectivity, reduction in traffic congestion and emissions, and the role of digital technologies in making cities more accessible, inclusive and liveable.
The Urban Mobility India Conference is an annual initiative of MoHUA under the National Urban Transport Policy (NUTP), 2006. The policy emphasises capacity building at the State and city levels and the development of equitable and sustainable urban transport systems. The Conference provides a platform for sharing national and international best practices, emerging technologies and innovative solutions in urban mobility.
Addressing the inaugural session,
Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu,
said that the Urban Mobility India Conference has emerged as an important national platform for shaping the future of urban transport. Highlighting this year’s theme, ‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’, he said that true progress in urban development should be measured by how safely, comfortably and independently citizens, including women, children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, can travel within cities.
Shri Sahu highlighted the significant expansion of metro rail infrastructure under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He stated that India’s operational metro network has expanded from 248 kilometres in 2014 to over 1,185 kilometres across 26 cities. He further informed that work is underway on another 998 kilometres of metro lines. He said that the expansion of metro networks, along with initiatives such as the National Common Mobility Card, QR-based ticketing and PM e-Bus Sewa, is transforming urban mobility and making public transport more accessible and sustainable.
Appreciating the efforts of the Government of Odisha, Shri Sahu highlighted the State’s Ama Bus services as an example of modern, technology-enabled public transport. He stated that efficient and inclusive urban mobility will play a crucial role in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He expressed confidence that the Conference would contribute to innovative solutions for making Indian cities more accessible, inclusive and environmentally sustainable.
Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra Hon’ble Minister,
Housing and Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha addressing the delegates and audience at UMI said “Urban mobility is not merely about transportation; it is about improving the quality of life of our citizens and making our cities more accessible, inclusive and sustainable. As Odisha’s cities continue to grow, our focus is on developing safe, reliable, affordable and people-centric public transport systems that respond to the everyday needs of citizens. Through initiatives such as Ama Bus and Ama E-Ride, we are taking meaningful steps towards making urban mobility more convenient and accessible for all, including students, working professionals, women and other commuters. The Urban Mobility India Conference 2026 provides a valuable platform for states and urban transport experts to exchange ideas, share best practices and explore innovative solutions for the future of our cities. We look forward to learning from these experiences and strengthening our collective efforts towards sustainable urban development and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Better Mobility, Better Lives is not just a vision, but a commitment to building cities where every citizen can travel with ease, safety and dignity.”
Speaking on the occasion Smt. Anu Garg, Chief
Secretary of Odisha stated “Odisha is committed to transforming urban mobility through the 8S approach—Service Access & Service Reliability, Smart Mobility, Sustainability, Systems, Safety, Seamlessness, Samaveshi  and Satisfaction. With around 800 buses serving eight cities, CRUT is strengthening public transport through digital ticketing, greater participation of women drivers and improved commuter convenience. Alongside expanding EV infrastructure, our focus is on building an integrated, inclusive and sustainable mobility ecosystem that makes public transport safer, smarter and accessible to all.”
Earlier, welcoming the dignitaries and delegates, Shri Satendra Singh,
Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA, said that the Urban Mobility India Conference, being held in Bhubaneswar for the first time, has evolved into an important international platform for sharing best practices and addressing challenges in urban transport since its inception in 2008.
Shri
Satendra Singh
informed that around 1,500 delegates from India and abroad are expected to participate in the two-day Conference, which includes technical sessions, round table discussions and research symposiums. He said that the deliberations would help shape policies and strategies for providing efficient, sustainable and high-quality urban transport solutions to India’s growing urban population.
Exhibition on Urban Transport Technologies and Best Practices
As part of the Conference, an exhibition showcasing best practices in urban transport from India and abroad, emerging technologies, services and innovative mobility solutions was inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu in the presence of Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra and other dignitaries.
A total of
28 exhibitors
, including representatives from the Government of Odisha, Metro Rail Companies, public sector organisations and private sector entities, are participating in the exhibition. The exhibition provides an opportunity to showcase technological advancements and exchange knowledge on sustainable urban transport solutions.
Technical Sessions and Deliberations
The first day of the Conference featured a Conclave Session, a Technical Session, three Round Table discussions and a Special Session on comprehensive regional mobility planning. The discussions covered the role of digital technology, data governance, institutional reforms and sustainable transport systems in improving urban accessibility and liveability.
The
Conclave Session on ‘Liveability, Mobility and Accessibility in Digital Age’
focused on the role of digital technologies in creating inclusive, connected and high-quality urban living environments. Discussions covered both physical mobility through different transport modes and digital connectivity that can reduce the need for physical travel. The session also examined accessibility of urban infrastructure for elderly persons and persons with disabilities. Deliberations highlighted scalable digital solutions and the integration of safety, privacy, accessibility and inclusivity into urban mobility systems.
The
Technical Session on ‘Data Governance and Intelligent Transport’
discussed the importance of reliable real-time data, common standards and data security in managing modern transport systems. The discussions covered the use of cameras, sensors, GPS and artificial intelligence for traffic management, improved safety and efficient transport operations. The session also examined data privacy, interoperability, public-private data exchange and the development of integrated mobility platforms for Indian cities.
The
Round Table on ‘Institutionalising Gender-Responsive Urban Planning’
deliberated on integrating gender-responsive approaches into urban planning frameworks, municipal regulations, budgets and institutional processes. The discussions highlighted the mobility needs of women and vulnerable groups. Emphasis was placed on gender-disaggregated data and the incorporation of inclusive mobility provisions in master plans, tenders and development regulations.
The
Round Table on ‘Modernizing Bus Systems – Role of SPVs and PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme: Lessons from CRUT’
examined approaches to improving urban bus services through dedicated Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) and technology-enabled transport management. The discussions focused on the PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme and the experience of Capital Region Urban Transport (CRUT), Odisha, in operating modern and inclusive bus systems. The session also covered challenges faced by cities in modernising bus operations and integrating different transport modes.
The
Round Table on ‘Transport, Air Quality and Public Health – Unlocking Clean Air Action through Low Emission Zone Policy’
focused on reducing transport-related pollution and improving public health in Indian cities. Discussions examined the potential of Low Emission Zones (LEZs) in encouraging cleaner vehicles and reducing exposure to harmful emissions. The session also covered legal, institutional, financial and technological requirements for implementing LEZs and approaches towards developing a National Low Emission Zone Strategy.
The
Special Session on ‘Comprehensive Regional Mobility Planning’
highlighted the experience of CRUT, Odisha, in integrating urban and regional public transport services. The discussions covered bus services operating under the Ama Bus/Mo Bus brand and feeder services such as Ama-E ride. The session examined regional transport integration across Bhubaneswar, Kataka, Khordha, Puri, Rourkela, Sambalpur and Berhampur. It also focused on integrated ticketing, technology-enabled operations and the challenges of providing seamless and sustainable mobility across expanding urban regions.
Research Symposium and Day-Two Programme
A Research Symposium is also being organised as part of the Conference to encourage young research scholars and PhD students to present their research work. A total of
46 research papers
have been selected through peer review. Of these, 20 papers will be presented by candidates, while the remaining 26 will be showcased through poster presentations. The three best research papers, selected by a jury, will receive cash awards of ₹25,000 each. Certificates will also be presented to all participants presenting their research.
The second day of the Conference, on 24 October 2026, will feature discussions on transit-oriented development, people-centric streets, behavioural change and public communication, intelligent and secure mobility, and rail-led integrated urban development.
The Conference will conclude with a valedictory session, during which awards for
‘Excellence/Best Practice Projects in Urban Transport’
will be presented to outstanding States, cities and transport organisations across different categories. Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, is scheduled to deliver the valedictory address and present the awards along with Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Odisha.
The 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition will be followed by the National Urban Conclave 2026, scheduled for 24–25 October 2026 at the same venue in Bhubaneswar.

title: DDWS Organises National-level Training of Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 to Strengthen Community-led Rural Drinking Water Management
subtitle: Story-based capacity-building package launched to strengthen grassroots leadership and sustainable management of village water supply systems
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised a National-level Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for State-Level Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 today at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. The programme brought together representatives from State Institutes of Rural Development (SIRDs), Public Health Engineering Departments (PHEDs), Rural Development institutions and other key stakeholders from State/UTs to strengthen capacities for large-scale community training and institutional development aimed at sustaining rural drinking water services across the country.
The training programme focused on the newly developed Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 Capacity Building Package comprising of 8 Modules titled
“The Story of Panipur:
A Story-Based self-learning Handbook on Rural Drinking Water Supply Management”
and a “
Trainer’s Facilitation Manual
”. The package has been designed to build the capacities of Gram Panchayat representatives, Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), Sujalam Shakti Groups and other grassroots institutions involved in the management and sustainability of rural drinking water services.
Delivering the keynote address,
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission
, stressed that the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems depends fundamentally on community ownership and institutional responsibility. The drinking water infrastructure being created today is intended to serve rural communities for the next several decades and therefore requires active participation of GPs, VWSCs and community groups from the very beginning.
He emphasised that achieving the
vision of Viksit Bharat 2047
would require not only creation of infrastructure but also sustained efforts to ensure its effective operation and maintenance through strong local institutions.
Referring to emerging examples of improved service delivery in several States, Shri Soan highlighted the need to prepare village institutions for progressively higher service standards and sustainable management of water supply systems. He urged participants to instil a strong sense of ownership among Panchayat representatives and community institutions so that drinking water infrastructure is viewed as a community asset that must be preserved and maintained collectively.
A key focus of his address was the convergence of JJM with Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), Panchayati Raj Institutions, Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) and dovetail from 16th Finance Commission tied grants and VB-G RAM G. He urged States to ensure that Panchayat representatives understand the financial resources and planning instruments available to them so that water source sustainability, operation and maintenance requirements and local drinking water priorities are adequately incorporated into development plans.
Shri Soan further highlighted the importance of user-charge collection, financial sustainability, source protection and community monitoring for ensuring the long-term functionality of rural water supply systems.
Calling for institutionalisation of the training programme, he urged States to
integrate the capacity-building modules into existing Rural Development and Panchayati Raj training systems
so that learning and capacity building continue beyond the Mission period and become part of a sustained support mechanism for rural drinking water service delivery.
Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation
, emphasised the critical importance of capacity building in ensuring the long-term success of the Mission. She observed that while significant investments are being made in creating rural drinking water infrastructure, the sustainability of these assets depends on informed communities and capable local institutions that can effectively operate, maintain and manage drinking water systems over time. Emphasising on the purpose of the training she said, it is not merely to impart technical knowledge but to enable trainers to communicate complex concepts in a simple, practical and relatable manner to village communities. She noted that the newly developed modules employ storytelling, folk communication methods, role plays, community interactions and gamification techniques to make learning more engaging and effective.
She highlighted that the ultimate objective of the initiative is to
strengthen community-led management of rural drinking water systems by building the capacities
. Village-level institutions are expected to play an increasingly important role in water distribution, operation and maintenance, user-charge management, grievance redressal, functionality monitoring and service improvement planning.
Smt. Naik also emphasised the importance of transparency and equitable access to information through digital platforms and dashboards, enabling citizens, Gram Panchayats and higher administrative levels to access programme information uniformly and participate more effectively in rural water governance. Noting that nearly 54 lakh stakeholders are proposed to be covered under the broader training programme, she urged State/UTs to establish robust dissemination mechanisms and training ecosystems to enable timely implementation.
Smt. Meena also highlighted the role of technology-enabled governance through initiatives such as Sujalam Bharat and layered dashboards. She emphasised that digital platforms should become tools for transparency, accountability and informed decision-making, enabling Gram Panchayats and citizens to actively monitor and improve service delivery. Emphasising the role of Sujalam Shakti Groups and noted that the initiative offers significant opportunities for women’s leadership, community mobilisation and livelihood enhancement while strengthening drinking water governance at the grassroots level.
In his concluding remarks,
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM
, emphasised that the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water services depends on community ownership, responsible water use and effective local management of water supply systems. He underlined the importance of protecting drinking water sources for future generations and called upon States to sensitise communities on water conservation, source sustainability and judicious water use as integral components of the capacity-building initiative.
Shri Soan highlighted that user charges should be viewed not merely as a financial mechanism, but as a tool for fostering responsibility and ownership among rural communities towards their drinking water systems. Stressing the distinction between water as a natural resource and drinking water service delivery, he observed that user contributions help communities appreciate the investments, operation and maintenance efforts involved in delivering safe drinking water to households and encourage greater participation in sustaining these services.
He further emphasised that while Panchayats should take a leading role in the day-to-day operation and management of village water supply systems, technical support from the concerned departments would continue to remain essential for addressing major repairs and technical challenges. Referring to the transformative impact of household tap water connections on dignity, convenience and equitable access to drinking water, he urged the participants to carry forward the key messages of community ownership, behavioural change, water conservation and institutional responsibility during the rollout of training programmes across States and Union Territories.
Resource persons from NJJM
viz.
Director, Deputy Secretary, Deputy Advisor and NPMU members
introduced the story-based self-learning handbook and Trainer’s Facilitation Manual and
delivered
the training.
The training package, built around the fictional village “
Panipur
”, comprises eight interconnected modules covering village water supply systems, source sustainability, water quality, institutional arrangements, operation and maintenance, digital governance, community ownership and the development of sustainable Sujal Gaons. The modules have been designed to promote participatory learning and help communities translate knowledge into practical action.
Representatives from partner organizations UNICEF and UNOPS shared their field experiences, key considerations, and practical approaches for preparing trainers and conducting effective grassroots-level training, while adhering to the prescribed module content and coordinating with SIRDs. They also assured that in their implementing states; they will support the state PHE/Rural Water Supply Department in delivering state-level and district-level trainings.
The National-level Training of Trainers marks an important step in operationalising the capacity-building architecture of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. By creating a strong network of State Master Trainers and equipping them with standardised training resources, the Mission seeks to strengthen Gram Panchayats, VWSCs and community institutions, deepen community ownership, and ensure the sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure and services across the country.

title: AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
subtitle:
India Advances Agrivoltaics Cooperation for the Global South

7th AgriVoltaics World Conference concludes with a call to accelerate farmer-centred solutions; France to host the 8th edition in 2027
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India brought the priorities of farmers and the Global South to the heart of the agrivoltaics dialogue as the 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference (AWC) 2026, hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, concluded here today. Three days of scientific exchange, farmer experiences and industry engagement sharpened the focus on a shared opportunity of using agricultural land to produce food and solar power, strengthen farm incomes and advance the clean energy transition.
The conference highlighted India’s contribution as a platform for connecting research, field experience and international partnerships. Policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, development partners and farmers examined how agrivoltaics can respond to the linked challenges of food security, energy access and climate resilience across India and the Global South.
The focus was firmly on implementation. Discussions examined agro-climatic zoning, crop selection, water-use efficiency, innovative financing and technology, with farmer-centred models at the core. The deliberations reinforced the need for solutions that countries can adapt to their own agricultural conditions and development priorities.
A session co-convened by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the International Water Management Institute (IWMI) examined how agro-climatic zoning can guide agrivoltaic deployment. Discussions covered shade-tolerant crops, water-use efficiency indices and the microclimatic impacts of solar arrays across different agro-climatic zones.
These exchanges placed scientific evidence at the centre of expansion. India’s engagement in this research dialogue offers a basis for wider knowledge exchange with Global South partners seeking to integrate solar power with productive agriculture. Location-specific evidence will be essential to identifying what works for farmers and where it can be deployed effectively.
A dedicated session led by GIZ brought progressive farmers, Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) federations and rural entrepreneurs into the discussion. Participants shared experiences from agrivoltaic installations, covering operational lessons, revenue diversification and maintenance practices.
Their message gave the deliberations a clear practical direction: project design must respond to farmers’ needs and field conditions. For India and other Global South countries, economically viable models that sustain agricultural production will be central to wider adoption. Farmer experience must help shape how projects are designed, financed and operated.
Presenting an overview of the conference proceedings and key outcomes, Shri Ashish Khanna, Director General, International Solar Alliance (ISA), highlighted opportunities to advance agrivoltaics through research, innovation and international collaboration.
Addressing participants at the closing ceremony, Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, MNRE, emphasised the importance of carrying the deliberations forward through continued collaboration and practical action.
The discussions brought renewed attention to the contribution India can make through shared learning and partnerships. Connecting Indian research and farmer experience with international expertise can help develop agrivoltaic approaches suited to diverse agricultural and energy needs across the Global South.
Dignitaries presented Excellence Awards recognising outstanding contributions to the agrivoltaics sector. The National Agrivoltaics Pitch-Hub Award recognised promising enterprise and start-up innovations with the potential to advance viable solutions.
Best Paper Awards across six scientific themes honoured research spanning system design, agronomy, monitoring, business models and socio-economic equity. The awards recognised the researchers, innovators and entrepreneurs working to turn scientific knowledge into practical advances for agriculture and renewable energy.
The closing ceremony marked the formal handover of hosting responsibility for the 8th AgriVoltaics World Conference in 2027 to France. The handover carried forward the momentum built in New Delhi and the continuing international effort to share knowledge, strengthen partnerships and advance agrivoltaic solutions across diverse farming contexts.
Ms. Taina Dyckhoff, Counsellor and Head of the Climate and Environment Division, Embassy of Germany in India, delivered the vote of thanks at the close of the ceremony.
New Delhi’s call to action was clear: bring agrivoltaics into the field through sound science, viable financing and sustained cooperation with farmers. By bringing these priorities together, India has helped strengthen a global dialogue rooted in the needs of the Global South. As the conference moves to France in 2027, the task ahead is to translate that momentum into solutions that make land more productive, diversify farmer incomes and expand clean energy for shared prosperity.

title: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances organises 22nd National e-Governance Webinar on Technology-enabled Governance in Public Safety and Rural Development

ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) organised the 22nd National e-Governance Webinar (NeGW) on 23 October 2026. The webinar was chaired by Shri Avanish Kumar Mishra, Joint Secretary, DARPG, and brought together officials from Central Ministries, State Governments, districts, local bodies, and temple and shrine management bodies to share approaches for technology-enabled governance.
The webinar showcased two Gold Award-winning initiatives recognised under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026: TRINETRA – AI-Based Video Surveillance System for the Mahakal Rudrasagar Integrated Development Area (MRIDA), including Mahakaleshwar Temple, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh; and the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) – Data-Driven Governance for Viksit Bharat, led by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. The initiatives demonstrated how AI-enabled surveillance and data analytics can support public safety, performance monitoring and evidence-based planning.
The National e-Governance Webinar Series provides a platform to disseminate award-winning e-Governance initiatives and support their adoption and replication, particularly at the State, district and local body levels.
TRINETRA – AI-Based Video Surveillance System
Shri Pratham Kaushik, (IAS) Administrator, Shri Mahakaleshwar Temple, Ujjain, presented TRINETRA, implemented for MRIDA in partnership with Ujjain Smart City Limited and the Shri Mahakaleshwar Temple Management Committee. The initiative adapts and scales the surveillance model of the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board to address the substantial increase in pilgrim footfall at Mahakaleshwar Temple and the surrounding area.
TRINETRA deploys more than 450 AI-enabled cameras, video analytics, facial recognition and predictive crowd monitoring through an Integrated Command & Control Centre. The system supports real-time surveillance, crowd-flow management and emergency response coordination. The project brief reports that emergency response time has reduced from 15–20 minutes to under five minutes. It also records 552 missing-person cases resolved, 53 lost items recovered, 10 theft incidents intercepted and video evidence provided in seven police cases.
The initiative provides a technology-enabled model for improving pilgrim safety and managing high-footfall religious and public congregation sites, while supporting future replication and scaling.
Panchayat Advancement Index – Data-Driven Governance for Viksit Bharat
Smt. Sunita Jain, Senior Director (IT), NIC, presented the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI), a data-driven framework of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj to assess Gram Panchayat performance across nine Localized Sustainable Development Goal (LSDG) themes. PAI uses standardised indicators, integrated data, validation workflows, analytical dashboards and Panchayat scorecards to assess development outcomes and identify priority areas for intervention.
The presentation on the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) highlighted its role in data-driven rural governance across nine development themes, using 150 indicators and 230 data points to identify gaps and guide targeted action. It enables officials at the village, block, district, State and Central levels to determine priorities, assign responsibilities and monitor progress. Designed as a development report card rather than merely a ranking exercise, the PAI portal covers around 2.6 lakh Gram Panchayats, supporting evidence-based planning and more targeted and sustainable rural development.
The webinar highlighted how the two initiatives apply technology and data to different governance contexts, strengthening safety and crowd management at a major pilgrimage destination and supporting transparent, measurable and evidence-based development at the grassroots. More than 360 officials participated in the session.
The session concluded by acknowledging the valuable contributions of the speakers and the active participation of officials and stakeholders. Participants were encouraged to consider the approaches presented for adoption and replication in their respective jurisdictions.

title: Capacity Building Commission was conceptualised by PM Narendra Modi ji who had initiated a series of governance reforms soon after he took over in 2014, says Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Dr. Jitendra Singh Says, Mission Karmayogi Marks Shift from Rule-Based to Role-Based Governance; Calls Training Institutions Key to Civil Services Transformation

At Lucknow, Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Yogi Adityanath ji Joins Dr. Jitendra Singh at Sadhana Shrinkhla Regional Workshop

Modi Govt’s Administrative Reforms Aim to Build a More Responsive, Citizen-Centric Governance System, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr Jitendra Singh lauds Uttar Pradesh for leading iGOT Karmayogi Participation with Over 19 Lakh Officials Registered:

Training Institutions Must Evolve into Centres of Excellence to Strengthen Civil Services Capacity Building: Dr. Jitendra Singh
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that Mission Karmayogi represents a fundamental shift in governance from a rule-based system to a role-based approach, equipping government officials with the competencies required to discharge their responsibilities effectively.
Addressing the third regional workshop of Sadhana Shrinkhla 2026 at Lucknow, the Minister said, Capacity Building Commission was conceptualised by PM Sh Narendra Modi ji who had initiated a series of governance reforms soon after he took over in 2024, and added that capacity building is central to the civil services transformation, with the ultimate objective of improving governance and public service delivery. He also lauded the Yogi Government for effective implementation of these governance reforms in Uttar Pradesh.
The two-day workshop, organised by the Capacity Building Commission in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh on October 23-24, brings together representatives from eight States and four Union Territories of the Northern Region to deliberate on transforming government training institutions into modern, competency-driven Capacity Building Institutions.
The workshop was graced by the presence of Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath. The programme was also attended by S. Radha Chauhan, Chairperson, Capacity Building Commission; Alka Mittal, Member, Capacity Building Commission; Shashi Prakash Goyal, Chief Secretary, Government of Uttar Pradesh; Devaraj, RUPAAM Director General Devaraj, Director Galong with senior officials of the Uttar Pradesh Government and representatives from various States and Union Territories.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the administrative reform journey initiated under Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2014 has focused on simplifying procedures, strengthening public trust and making governance more accessible. Citing the removal of the requirement for gazetted officers to attest documents and the discontinuation of interviews for certain government recruitment processes, he said these measures reflected confidence in citizens and a commitment to fairness in public administration. He also referred to Rozgar Melas, CPGRAMS and Digital Life Certificates as examples of reforms that have simplified procedures and improved the delivery of public services.
Referring to CPGRAMS, the Minister said that annual public grievance registrations had increased from around two lakhs in 2014 to approximately 25 lakhs, reflecting greater public confidence in the grievance-redressal mechanism. With around 95–97 per cent of grievances being disposed of in a time-bound manner, citizens increasingly expect their concerns to receive a response. He also spoke about Digital Life Certificates, including the use of biometric and facial-recognition technologies, which have eased compliance for pensioners and reduced the need for cumbersome physical procedures.
The Minister said that the Capacity Building Commission represents an important institutional step in this reform journey. Capacity building must prepare government employees to move beyond routine file processing and develop the competencies required to perform their roles effectively. The objective, he said, is to create a civil service that is equipped to take responsibility, adapt to changing requirements and deliver tangible improvements in governance.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that government training institutions must become central to this transformation. Traditionally custodians of institutional knowledge and experience, they need to evolve beyond delivering conventional training programmes and become Capacity Building Institutions that respond systematically to the competency requirements of government.
A structured framework can help them strengthen institutional governance and faculty capabilities, improve curricula and pedagogy, build partnerships, adopt technology and assess the outcomes of their interventions. Over time, this would enable institutions to develop specialised expertise and emerge as Centres of Excellence.
Referring to the principles of Tradition, Technology and Tangible Outcomes, the Minister said that these three elements provide a practical direction for strengthening capacity building under Mission Karmayogi. Training institutions represent tradition through accumulated knowledge and institutional experience; iGOT Karmayogi enables technology-driven learning at scale; and Human Resource Management Systems can connect competencies with the professional journeys and deployment of officials.
Integrating these elements can help government align the competencies required for a role with the learning undertaken by an official and the responsibilities subsequently assigned, giving practical meaning to the shift from rule to role.
The Minister congratulated Uttar Pradesh for its performance in implementing capacity-building initiatives. He said that more than 19 lakh officials and employees from the State had registered on iGOT Karmayogi, contributing to national participation of approximately 1.7 crore.
He also drew attention to the popularity of courses on Yoga and Artificial Intelligence among learners from Uttar Pradesh, describing this combination as an example of how traditional knowledge and modern technology can advance together. He commended the State administration for its efforts and said its performance could inspire other States.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also appreciated Uttar Pradesh’s contribution to UNNATI, the Unified New Age National Training Initiative, which connects training institutions to facilitate collaboration, resource sharing and alignment with government’s capacity-building requirements.
Referring to the figures cited during his address, he said that more than 370 training institutions from Uttar Pradesh had joined the initiative, against around 110 institutions nationally. He said that a stronger network of training institutions would support the exchange of expertise and good governance practices across States.
The Minister said that the success of capacity-building initiatives must ultimately be measured by their impact on the ground, rather than merely by the number of training programmes conducted or officials trained. Their contribution should be reflected in the competencies developed, institutional leadership nurtured and improvements achieved in government performance.
He added that training institutions should increasingly serve as centres of learning, mentorship and leadership development, working with academic institutions, industry and practitioners while remaining focused on citizen-centric governance.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also commended Uttar Pradesh for its contribution to good governance initiatives, recalling the State’s participation in the Good Governance Index and regional efforts to disseminate effective administrative practices. He expressed confidence that, under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh would continue to serve as a model for sharing good governance practices with other States and Union Territories.
The Minister expressed gratitude to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for his support and for facilitating the Sādhana Śhrinkhla workshop in Uttar Pradesh. He said the initiative provided an opportunity to bring together States and Union Territories to advance the transformation of government training institutions and strengthen the capacity of civil servants to deliver effective, accountable and citizen-centric governance.

title: Union Minister for Railways and Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh to Inaugurate Satna–Devendra Nagar (53 km) and Rewa–Churhat (65 km) Rail Sections Tomorrow
subtitle:
Devendra Nagar–Churhat Train Service to Be Flagged Off; Sidhi District to Be Connected to Rail Network for the First Time Since Independence

Expansion of Rail Connectivity in the Vindhya Region to Boost Industry, Trade, Tourism and Employment
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A significant milestone in the expansion of rail connectivity in the Vindhya region of Madhya Pradesh is set to be achieved on 24 October 2026. Hon’ble Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav will inaugurate the Satna–Devendra Nagar (53 km) and Rewa–Churhat (65 km) rail sections, covering a total of 118 kilometres of railway line. The new Devendra Nagar–Churhat train service will also be flagged off on the occasion.
The connection of Sidhi district to the rail network for the first time since Independence is a historic achievement for the Vindhya region. It will give a boost to passenger movement and freight transportation while creating new opportunities for industrial activities, trade and employment. A record budget allocation of ₹15,188 crore has been made for railway development in Madhya Pradesh in the financial year 2026–27, while railway projects worth approximately ₹1,18,379 crore are currently in progress in the state.
The Lalitpur–Singrauli New Rail Line Project is of particular importance to the Vindhya region. The project will expand the rail network and strengthen connectivity to areas such as Panna, Satna, Rewa, Sidhi and Singrauli. Upon completion, it will help connect mineral-rich regions with major industrial and transportation hubs across the country.
The programme at Churhat Railway Station will be attended by Shri Rajendra Shukla, Deputy Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Janardan Mishra, Member of Parliament from Rewa; Shri Rajesh Mishra, Member of Parliament from Sidhi; and other public representatives and dignitaries.
The programme at Nagod Railway Station will be attended by Smt. Pratima Bagri, Minister of State in the Government of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Ganesh Singh, Member of Parliament from Satna; Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma, Member of Parliament from Khajuraho; Shri Nagendra Singh, MLA from Nagod; and other public representatives and dignitaries.
Satna–Devendra Nagar Rail Section
Developed under the Lalitpur–Singrauli New Rail Line Project, this rail section will strengthen connectivity to Satna, Nagod, Devendra Nagar and surrounding areas. Improved rail connectivity will make transportation easier and promote the development of limestone-based industries and cement plants. It will also support local trade, industrial activities, education and employment opportunities.
Rewa–Churhat Rail Section
This 65-kilometre-long rail section will further strengthen rail connectivity between the Rewa and Sidhi regions. Several important engineering works, including railway bridges and tunnels, have been undertaken across the hilly terrain along this route. These include a 3.33-kilometre-long tunnel.
With the development of this rail section, Sidhi district has been connected to the rail network for the first time. Given the availability of limestone and other minerals in the region, the route is also expected to be useful for transporting cement, clinker and other freight in the future.
New Train Service to Benefit Passengers
The introduction of the Devendra Nagar–Churhat train service will provide an additional travel option for local passengers, students, employees and traders. It will improve connectivity between surrounding areas and support activities related to education, trade and employment.
Tourism to Receive a Boost
The development of the Satna–Devendra Nagar and Rewa–Churhat rail sections is expected to give fresh impetus to tourism across the Vindhya region. The area is home to several prominent tourist attractions, including the White Tiger Safari at Mukundpur.
Improved rail connectivity will make it more convenient for tourists to access the region’s religious, historical and natural attractions. This will boost tourism, local trade, hotels and transport services while creating new employment opportunities in the region.
The development of these rail sections will facilitate the expansion of industrial activities, the establishment of new industries and cement plants, and the creation of local employment opportunities across the Vindhya region. Better rail connectivity will ease freight transportation, encourage trade and help expand employment opportunities for local youth. Thus, the expansion of the rail network will provide fresh impetus to regional economic development and public welfare.

In a path-breaking initiative to enhance citizen-centric services along National Highways, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued guidelines for the upgradation, maintenance and smart monitoring of public toilet facilities and designated parking areas at toll plazas. The guidelines prescribe standards for upgrading existing facilities, regular cleaning, technology-enabled monitoring, citizen feedback and performance-based accountability to ensure clean, safe and functional public facilities for National Highway users.
Comprehensive Upgradation and Maintenance
Existing toilet facilities will undergo technical assessment before rehabilitation to identify necessary repairs and replacements. Upgradation will cover flooring, plumbing, sanitary fittings, lighting, ventilation, drainage, signage and other essential amenities. Housekeeping requirements and cleaning schedules will be based on the size of toilet blocks and traffic levels to ensure regular maintenance and availability of basic amenities.
Focus on Safety and Accessibility
The guidelines provide adequate measures to ensure safety for female highway users and families stopping at night that include proper lighting, CCTV surveillance of approaches and parking areas, sanitary napkin vending machines and clearly visible information signs indicating the availability of public amenities. Each covered toll plaza must also provide at least one universally accessible toilet unit with barrier-free access, suitable doorways and grab bars for people with disabilities.
Parking areas at the toll plazas will be improved through designated parking bays and proper drainage, with provisions for future Electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
Smart Monitoring and Citizen Feedback
Technology-based monitoring will help track water availability, odour, sewage levels, leakages, electricity supply and toilet occupancy. Alerts for issues such as water shortages, sewage overflow and equipment failures will enable timely corrective action. Smart Monitoring data will be integrated with NHAI’s central digital platform to help officials track facility conditions, maintenance, complaints and agency performance through a digitalized central dashboard.
National Highway users will be able to share feedback through QR codes linked to the
Rajmargyatra app
and touchscreens at toilet facilities. Digitally recorded complaints and suggestions will help authorities monitor issues and their resolution.
In addition, cleaning and desludging of septic tanks, soak pits and sewer lines have been mandated to be carried out using completely mechanised desludging methods. Manual entry into septic tanks, manholes and sewer lines will be strictly prohibited.
Performance-Based Accountability
The guidelines establish a structured inspection framework comprising daily supervision, weekly technical inspections, monthly joint reviews, quarterly audits and annual third-party assessments. Performance will be assessed through physical inspections, monitoring data and verified citizen feedback. The guidelines set clear deadlines for fixing problems and financial penalties if facilities are not maintained properly. Agencies that repeatedly fail to meet the required standards may face strict action.
Through these measures, NHAI aims to improve the upkeep of public amenities at toll plazas and ensure cleaner, safer and more accessible facilities through transparent, technology-enabled monitoring and accountability.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Enhanced NMMS App Version with Advanced Security Features for VB-G RAM G
subtitle:
New version developed with IIT Madras support strengthens attendance verification, safeguards workers’ wages and addresses network connectivity challenges

Nearly 46 crore person-days generated under VB-G RAM G; 10.997 crore Farmer IDs created, taking India close to the 11-crore milestone ahead of the December 2027 target
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 OCT 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today launched an enhanced, security-focused version of the National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS) app for recording workers’ attendance under the VB-G RAM G. Developed with technical support from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras and relevant technical agencies, the upgraded version introduces stronger device-level security, AI-based verification and safeguards against app tampering and fraudulent attendance. It also provides for offline attendance recording in areas without network connectivity and an exception mechanism for genuine workers facing authentication difficulties. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Shri Chouhan said the government’s priority was to ensure employment for rural workers, protect their wages and ensure that public funds were used transparently and for their intended purpose. He emphasised that technology must strengthen accountability without allowing genuine workers to be denied their entitlements because of connectivity or technical problems. Rural Development Secretary Rohit Kansal, Joint Secretary Rohini R. Bhajibhakre and other officials were present at the event.
VB-G RAM G generates nearly 46 crore person-days
Shri Chouhan said the vision of Viksit Bharat is being advanced alongside efforts to build developed villages across the country. The VB-G RAM G scheme, implemented across all rural areas from July 1, 2026, has provided employment support to rural households, he said. Sharing the scheme’s progress, the Minister said work had been undertaken at 31.23 lakh worksites across more than 2.41 lakh Gram Panchayats. In response to demand, employment had been provided to more than 3.65 crore workers belonging to 2.89 crore rural households. Nearly 46 crore person-days have been generated so far, of which approximately 40 crore have been recorded through face authentication, he said. The Centre has allocated ₹95,692 crore for the scheme in the financial year 2026-27. Including the states’ share, the total provision exceeds ₹1.51 lakh crore. A mother sanction of ₹26,126 crore has already been issued to states and Union Territories as the first instalment.
Enhanced face authentication to curb fraudulent attendance
The Union Minister said complaints of fake attendance and wages being claimed in the names of other individuals had necessitated stronger verification measures. Face authentication was introduced in the NMMS app in March 2026 to address these concerns. Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand have achieved 100% attendance recording through face authentication at worksites, he said. The system has helped substantially reduce the scope for impersonation and fraudulent entries. The latest version builds on a security update released in the last week of September 2026. Shri Chouhan said cybersecurity required continuous improvement to keep pace with evolving attempts at technological breaches. The upgraded app integrates Google Play Integrity and incorporates device-level security checks, secure data transmission, safeguards against cloning and tampering, and liveness detection. These features are designed to verify that the person appearing before the camera is a real, live worker rather than a dummy image or an old photograph. AI-based face verification has also been refined to account for differences across states and geographical regions.
Offline attendance and exception mechanism to protect genuine workers
Emphasising that technological safeguards must not come at the expense of workers’ rights, Shri Chouhan said no genuine worker should lose employment or wages because of poor network connectivity or technical difficulties. Where network connectivity is unavailable at a worksite, attendance can be recorded offline under the prescribed procedure and uploaded once the device reaches an area with network access, after the muster roll is closed. An authorised exception mechanism is also available when face authentication fails for elderly workers or persons with disabilities, or when a mobile device encounters technical problems. In such cases, the mate or field worker can submit a request under the prescribed process.
Multi-layered checks before wage payments
Shri Chouhan explained that recording attendance through the app alone does not automatically determine wage payments. A multi-layered verification system is in place to ensure that payments correspond to genuine work. The system includes an AI-based photo de-duplication module that identifies suspicious or repeated photographs. Where such entries are detected, the wage list and Fund Transfer Order (FTO) are automatically withheld until the necessary checks are completed. The electronic Measurement Book (e-MB) records the actual work carried out at the site, as physically measured by technical engineers. Wage amounts are determined on the basis of this measurement, following which payments are transferred directly to workers’ bank accounts through the prescribed Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) process. This ensures traceability of transactions. The Minister said random spot inspection teams had been deployed in districts to verify the authenticity of work on the ground. Social audits and public disclosure mechanisms have also been implemented. States have been directed to closely monitor the use of suspicious or unauthorised applications. Where such misuse is detected, they have been instructed to collect digital evidence promptly and initiate criminal proceedings under the applicable laws. Chouhan reiterated that employment would be provided to those who need it, but corruption and irregularities would not be tolerated.
Farmer ID drive nears 11-crore milestone ahead of deadline
Sharing an update on another major initiative aimed at improving agricultural service delivery, Shri Chouhan said the nationwide Farmer ID drive was progressing rapidly to expand the use of technology in agriculture and make government schemes more accessible to farmers. Under the target set by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, 11 crore Farmer IDs are to be created by December 2027. India has already generated 10 crore 99 lakh 70 thousand Farmer IDs, bringing the country within 30,000 IDs of the 11-crore milestone more than a year ahead of the deadline. Shri Chouhan said the achievement marked significant progress towards technology-enabled agricultural services and easier access to government schemes for farmers.
